papers.abstract: Human urine represents a nutrient-rich reservoir that, if recycled, could significantly offset global fertilizer demands. Yet, its potential remains largely underexploited because rapid urea hydrolysis at the source drives N and P losses via uncontrolled precipitation, while causing pipe clogging and malodor formation. Here, we report a wollastonite (CaSiO3)-integrated electrochemical alkalization and oxidation (EAO) system that enables concurrent urea stabilization and phosphorus recovery. Anodic proton-driven dissolution of CaSiO3 releases Ca2+, which combines with cathodically generated alkalinity to promote phosphate precipitation, whereas anodic oxidation suppresses urease-mediated urea hydrolysis. We show that the driving force lies in the microenvironment near the electrode, which has distinct pH, Ca2+ and active‑chlorine gradients. Treating two‑fold diluted urine at 12 A m-2 yields the most energy‑efficient scenario (20.11 kWh kg-1 P, 2.99 kWh m-3 urine), achieving 96.0% phosphate recovery and robust urea stabilization in real urine. We expect the EAO system to create a scalable electrochemical route to close nutrient loops in decentralized sanitation, supporting sustainable fertilizer production and urine management.

papers.abstract: This study reports a series of CRBN molecular glues that selectively induce proteasomal degradation of VAV1, a hematopoietic-specific signaling protein and key target in hematological malignancies and autoimmune diseases. Using unbiased global proteomics, we identify phenyl-glutarimide derivatives (e.g., NGT-201-12) as effective VAV1 degraders that engage its C-terminal SH3 domain (SH3-2). We elucidate a non-canonical RT-loop degron (RDxS motif, residues 796-799) in SH3-2, distinct from previously characterized G-loop degrons, supported by the physics- and AI-driven GluePlex workflow and site-directed mutagenesis. Applying Free Energy Perturbation (FEP) to predicted ternary structures yields cooperativity metrics that correlate with degradation potency, overcoming limitations of standard docking and enabling prospective ranking of analogs-even from weak initial binders. We further show that conformational restriction via halogen substitution (e.g., NGT-201-18) potentiates degradation, a principle rationalized by DFT calculations, while comprehensive SAR studies chart a roadmap for next-generation degraders. Dose-response proteomics confirms VAV1 as the primary target and reveals LIMD1, bearing a canonical G-loop, as an off-target, showing that one glue can engage disparate degrons. These findings expand the landscape of CRBN neosubstrate recognition and offer a therapeutic strategy for targeting VAV1.

papers.abstract: The plant hormone jasmonoyl-isoleucine (JA-Ile) reallocates resources from growth towards induced defenses upon microbial or herbivore attacks or other environmental threats. JA-Ile and its precursor jasmonic acid (JA) undergo complex enzymatic turnover that shape hormonal dynamics for optimal signaling. JA-Ile is inactivated through gradual oxidation by CYP94 monooxygenases, followed by 12-OH-JA-Ile deconjugation towards 12-OH-JA. 12-OH-JA was believed to originate also from direct JA hydroxylation by JAO/JOX dioxygenases. Here we investigate the nature and origins of hydroxy-JAs and their derivatives upon stress responses in Arabidopsis. Using a set of analytical methods to explore enzyme assays and multiple pathway-impaired mutants, we show that JAO enzymes produce exclusively 11-OH-JA rather than 12-OH-JA and define a separate branch in JA catabolism. Upon leaf wounding, the CYP94/AH and, to a lesser extent, the JAO pathways direct the respective accumulation of 12- and 11-OH-JAs and their 11/12-glucosylated and 12-sulfated derivatives with isoform-specific occurrences. In contrast, Botrytis infection triggers the exclusive accumulation of 11-OH-JA and 11-Glc-O-JA with complex patterns of HSO4-JA. Finally, treatment of jar1 seedlings with 11-OH-JA does not trigger transcriptional changes, reinforcing the notion that the JAO/11-OH-JA pathway represents a metabolic sink modulating JA-Ile formation. Our findings elucidate the 11-OH-JA biosynthetic pathway and highlight stress-specific hydroxylation signatures.

papers.abstract: Wireless body sensor networks could enable unencumbered human-machine interfaces for robotics, assistive healthcare, and immersive computing. However, their widespread adoption remains constrained by bulky batteries and inefficient wireless communication. Here, we report a battery-free wireless body sensor network enabled by a dual-mode metamaterial textile for continuous and unobtrusive human-machine interactions. The textile, digitally embroidered with liquid-metal fibers, establishes ultra-wideband electromagnetic pathways to simultaneously support efficient near-field power transfer and Bluetooth communication across the entire human body. This architecture enhances data throughput by 37.8 times and doubles wireless power transfer efficiency compared with emerging near-field clothing. When worn, the metamaterial-integrated clothing allows an NFC-enabled smartphone to serve as a central hub, wirelessly delivering power to and acquiring multimodal signals from distributed battery-free HMI sensors. We demonstrate that this battery-free body sensor network remains robust during motion and enables intuitive, unencumbered interactions in robotic control, virtual reality, and human digital twins.

papers.abstract: Polyploidy, the possession of more than two sets of chromosomes in somatic cells, is a major driver in the diversification of flowering plants. Whereas an association between the occurrence of polyploids and latitude suggests a major impact of temperature on their global distribution, it remains unknown how polyploid frequency varies at regional spatial scales, leaving unclear the overall robustness of such relationship and its major determinants. Here, we present a flora-wide dataset of newly sampled, georeferenced ploidy occurrence data for ca. 42,000 samples of angiosperms collected along 101 elevational transects across the Eastern European Alps. Based on these data, we find that on a regional level polyploid frequency decreases with elevation, in contrast to expectations derived from global latitudinal distribution patterns. Moreover, polyploid frequency increases with distance from glacial refugia for samples below the timberline, particularly for plants with limited dispersal abilities. These results suggest that range dynamics associated with Pleistocene climatic fluctuations rather than current temperature may have played a predominant role for the current distribution of polyploids in temperate mountain ranges. In sum, our systematic fine-scale survey identified a complex interplay between historical processes and current environments on polyploid distribution that have remained undetected at the global scale.

papers.abstract: Through cumulative cultural evolution, human populations discover novel solutions that allow them to solve complex problems. However, populations also reliably develop and sustain practices that are costly yet appear to have no effect on their stated outcome, such as bloodletting, divination, and malicious sorcery. Here, we show that ineffective, costly solutions can develop and be maintained because of their cognitive appeal. In a pre-registered transmission-chain experiment, participants were tasked with developing a solution to a problem over several trials, after which they passed instructions onto the subsequent generation. The visual appearance of the experimental task was manipulated to vary the extent to which cognitive biases could interfere with participants' expectations of efficacy, enabling a direct test of the effect of cognitive appeal on cumulative cultural evolution. Participants in the low-appeal treatment (n = 240) progressively develop more efficient solutions across generations. Participants in the high-appeal treatment (n = 240), in contrast, produce costlier solutions, and we did not observe a statistically significant increase in efficiency over the course of the experiment. These results suggest that, even under conditions favorable to cumulative cultural evolution, a form of cognitive appeal can alone prevent the process and promote the emergence and cultural persistence of ineffective solutions.

papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) metal oxides (MOs) are crucial materials in semiconductor optoelectronics and energy applications. Recently, ultra-confined and anisotropic polaritons, which are hybrid light-matter waves, in 2D MOs have renewed interest in the field of nanophotonics. With natural abundance, diverse compositions, and rich symmetries, MOs exhibit a wide range of electromagnetic responses from the visible to terahertz spectral range, providing various polariton platforms for designing on-chip photonic integrated circuits. In this Review, we discuss crystal symmetry and polaritons in MOs, present intrinsic and extrinsic manipulation approaches, and summarize strategies for synthesizing 2D polaritonic MOs. We also propose 2D MO-based polaritonic device architectures for use in heat management, photonics, and biosensing, all of which could be integrated into future photonic chips. Overall, with the rapid flourishing of 2D MO polaritonics, this review aims to stimulate further exploration and innovation for next-generation on-chip photonic systems.

papers.abstract: Despite dramatic human-driven changes across ecosystems, local-scale aggregate biodiversity metrics are often surprisingly stable, even as communities experience substantial reorganization of species identities and relative abundances. While rare species are often thought to be more vulnerable to these changes, emerging evidence suggests that common species may experience disproportionately greater declines. To evaluate these alternatives, we synthesize population trends for species initially rare or common across assemblages from 4748 sites within 129 studies spanning terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. We quantify how population trends relate to initial abundances using hierarchical Bayesian models that account for regression to the mean and include realm, taxon, and environmental covariates. We find consistently stronger declines among formerly common species in marine and terrestrial assemblages, while freshwater assemblages show no clear directional pattern. Rare species present at the start also decline, but less so than common species, while colonists that were not present at the start of the time series compensate for losses within the rarest abundance category. Climate change and anthropogenic drivers modulate these trends, with increasing temperature and non-climatic human pressures attenuating losses of initially common species, particularly in marine systems. Overall, we find widespread declines in common species through time, with potential functional consequences.

papers.abstract: Palladium plays a three-fold role in modern science and technology: it serves as a key active center in modern catalytic synthetic methods, occurs as unwanted trace contamination that influences new catalysts development and can lead to false-positive reports, and is an emerging environmental pollutant from automotive catalysts. High activity at ppm/ppb loadings and the necessity to analyze sub-micromolar concentrations of samples are common challenges in these applications, making reliable Pd identification essential. Mass spectrometry (MS) can detect Pd-containing ions in complex mixtures, but post-spectral recognition is difficult when minor Pd signals overlap with signals from other components and fine isotope structures are not visible. The present study introduces a machine-learning-based (ML) approach featuring a graph algorithm for the separation of signals from different multicharged ions and deep-learning classifiers for the automatic recognition of Pd ions in mass spectra of multi-component mixtures down to 10-8 mol L-1. It is applied to Pd intermediates in catalytic synthesis, contaminant catalysis and environmental samples. The scalability of the approach enables extension to Ni, Cu, Ag, Cl and Br. With the developed ML/MS workflow, Pd and other important elements could be automatically revealed; thus, routine MS hardware could be transformed into high-performance scanners.

papers.abstract: Conventional waveguide optical resonators face inherent limitations of low damage thresholds, limited coupling tunability, and stochastic resonance. To overcome these, we introduce a geometrical-optics resonator (GOR) framework, emulating free-space reflection and thin-film coupling on-chip. Using ultra-wide waveguides with total internal reflection (TIR) mirrors and frustrated-TIR couplers, GORs eliminate conventional constraints. Fabricated devices achieve intrinsic Q-factors >1 million and enable tunable microwave photonic filters operating distortion-free at about 10× higher optical power. Design flexibility allows precisely tuned coupled resonators, facilitating cascaded networks for spectral engineering. Demonstrated GOR photonic molecules exhibit dynamically adjustable mode splitting (0.49 free spectral range), nearing theoretical limits. The platform also realizes record-large-scale Floquet topological photonic insulators with 1281 GOR lattices, supporting robust edge modes against defects and a broadband continuum. The GOR sets new performance benchmarks, enabling scalable platforms for quantum simulation and topological networks while driving integrated photonics toward higher density and system-level integration.

papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskite quantum dots (QDs) are promising materials for developing low-cost and high-performance quantum dot-based light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). Despite external quantum efficiency (EQE) comparable to II-VI/III-V QLEDs, perovskite QD counterparts achieve peak EQE at low luminance/current density and exhibit significantly more pronounced efficiency roll-off, owing primarily to their ionic character and soft lattice. Engineering a robust surface is essential to ensure the structural stability of perovskite QDs, yet achieving this remains a critical challenge. Here, we develop an H2S-mediated surface passivation strategy. Experimental measurements confirm Pb-S coordination and a reduction in oleylamine ligand density, while DFT calculations suggest that (H2S)2 dimers may additionally interact with Cs-vacancy-related surface environments. This H2S-induced surface reconstruction creates a more robust surface coordination environment in CsPbI3 QDs. Benefiting from the enhanced surface stability, LEDs incorporating the treated CsPbI3 QDs possess increased ion migration barrier, balanced charge injection, and suppressed Auger recombination. These combined improvements yield a peak EQE of 30.71% at 52 mA cm-2 and 91.46 W Sr-1 m-2, with the device maintaining EQEs of 18.59% at ~500 mA cm-2 and 21.15% at ~500 W Sr-1 m-2, as well as an operational half-lifetime of 104,587 h.

papers.abstract: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics (STT) integrates spatially resolved gene expression with temporal information derived from staged samples, paired treatment specimens, or computational inference, providing a framework for reconstructing tissue-level dynamics. In the tumour microenvironment (TME), STT extends static molecular and cellular maps by revealing how cellular neighbourhoods and functional niches are reorganised during tumour evolution. This review examines how STT characterises TME remodelling during malignant transformation, invasion, metastasis, ageing, and treatment response. We discuss strategies for resolving temporal dynamics, including stage-stratified sampling, paired or serial specimens, pseudotime and trajectory inference, and complementary intravital imaging. We further consider how spatiotemporal analyses can connect changes in cellular states, spatial organisation, and intercellular interactions with clinically relevant tumour phenotypes. By linking the spatial organisation of the TME with stage- and treatment-associated molecular changes, STT may improve the prioritisation of candidate targets, treatment stratification, and the development of precision oncology strategies.

papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to verify that a strategy involving prophylactic exposure of the inferior parathyroid glands and preservation of their venous blood flow-achieved through early identification and protection of their venous drainage-can enhance the success rate of maintaining glandular perfusion and effectively reduce the incidence of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. This study included 600 patients who underwent total thyroidectomy with concomitant bilateral central neck dissection between November 2019 and December 2025. Patients were divided into two groups based on the surgical technique: Group A (n = 244), in which a prophylactic approach was used to protect the venous drainage of the inferior parathyroid glands, and Group B (n = 356), which underwent conventional in situ preservation of the inferior parathyroid glands. A comparison was made between the two groups regarding both the percentage of inferior parathyroid glands successfully preserved in situ and the incidence of postoperative hypoparathyroidism. The rate of visualization of inferior parathyroid glands with optimal blood supply was significantly higher in Group A than in Group B (p < 0.001). Postoperation parathyroid hormone level in Group A was significantly higher than that in Group B (25.15 [19.39, 33.58] pg/mL vs. 19.12 [9.82, 28.85] pg/mL, p < 0.001). In Group A, the rates of postoperative hypoparathyroidism-encompassing both transient and permanent forms-were significantly lower than those in Group B (p < 0.001). The method of prophylactically exposing the inferior parathyroid glands and preserving their venous system-termed prophylactic preservation of inferior parathyroid venous blood flow-is achieved through early identification and protection of their venous drainage. This approach enhances the success rate of maintaining glandular blood supply and effectively reduces the incidence of postoperative hypoparathyroidism.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) mortality disparities are partly driven by unequal access to care. Transportation barriers may limit access to definitive treatment. We studied how driving travel time affects receipt of definitive PCa treatment. We conducted a cohort study of men with non-metastatic PCa (2000-2015; follow-up through 2018) across the metropolitan area cancer registries of seven US states. Travel time was estimated using Google Maps isochrones representing driving time thresholds to reach the hospital appended to geomasked residential addresses. Outcomes were "no treatment," "radical surgery," or "radiotherapy". Covariate-adjusted multinomial logistic regression with interaction terms assessed modification by sociodemographic factors. The study included 132,939 men, of whom 37.0% received no treatment, 41.0% underwent surgery, and 22.0% received radiotherapy. Longer driving time (≥ 90 min vs. < 30 min) was associated with higher radical prostatectomy (aOR: 1.08, 95% CI: 1.03, 1.12), but lower radiotherapy (0.72, 95% CI: 0.69-0.76). Subgroup analyses revealed higher surgery associated with longer driving times among those in nSES Q1 (aOR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.21-1.45) vs. Q5 (aOR: 0.94, 95% CI: 0.86-1.04), those in low (aOR: 1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.24) vs. high (aOR: 1.03, 95% CI: 0.98-1.09) population density areas, and those with regional (aOR: 1.30, 95% CI: 1.14-1.48) vs. localized (aOR: 1.05, 95% CI: 1.00-1.09) disease. Longer driving time was mostly associated with lower odds of radiotherapy across sociodemographic subgroups. Higher travel time was associated with lower radiotherapy receipt, but higher surgery use in deprived and rural patients, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract: Venetoclax (VEN)-based regimens improve remission in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but infectious toxicity remains a concern. We compared infection profiles under VEN-based versus conventional therapy in newly diagnosed, non-M3 AML at a single tertiary center (2015-2024; n = 358; VEN = 156; non-VEN = 202). After 1:1 propensity-score matching on nine baseline covariates (115 per group), we assessed infection rates and event density (events per 1000 person-days) by site and pathogen, time to first infection (120-day cumulative incidence), and landmark associations between early infections and progression-free survival (PFS). Baseline predictors of microbiologically documented infection (MDI) were modeled in the pre-matching cohort. VEN was associated with higher febrile-neutropenia (FN) event density (IRR, 1.77; 95% CI, 1.33-2.36; p < 0.001; 16.40 vs. 9.27 per 1000 person-days). Site-level patterns diverged: upper-respiratory and lung infections showed lower first-event incidence with VEN, whereas skin/soft-tissue and perianal sites showed higher event density without higher patient-level incidence. By pathogen, bacterial and fungal first events were fewer with VEN while event densities were comparable; viral infections occurred earlier and accrued higher cumulative incidence. Cumulatively, the first infection was lower with VEN at days 30, 60, and 90 but converged by day 120. In the pre-matching cohort, higher HCT-CI (1-2/≥ 3 vs. 0) and higher DBIL independently predicted MDI, while female sex predicted lower risk. MDIs within 90 days-bacterial/fungal-driven-were associated with inferior PFS at 100 and 365 days, whereas early viral infections showed no association.

papers.abstract: Household size and composition may be associated with health-related quality of life (HRQoL), yet these associations remain poorly characterized among cancer survivors. We examined how household adult composition and presence of children were associated with HRQoL among U.S. cancer survivors. Adult (aged ≥ 18 years) cancer survivors were included from the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) 2017-2024. Household composition was defined by number of adults (1, 2, or ≥ 3) and presence of children (none vs. ≥ 1). Outcomes included poor physical health (PPH), poor mental health (PMH; each defined as ≥ 14 days/month), and fair/poor general health. Multivariable Poisson regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals. Among 138,360 cancer survivors, 45.2% (n = 62,605) resided in single-adult households, 47.1% (n = 65,132) in two-adult households, and 7.7% (n = 10,623) in households with ≥ 3 adults; children were present in 5.1% (n = 7063) of households. After adjustment, two-adult household residence was associated with lower prevalence of poor physical health (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 0.93, 95% CI 0.87-0.99), poor mental health (aPR 0.90, 95% CI 0.82-0.98), and fair/poor general health (aPR 0.92, 95% CI 0.88-0.97; all p ≤ 0.019) compared with single-adult households. Residence with ≥ 3 adults and child presence was not associated with any examined HRQoL outcome after adjustment. Exploratory stratified analyses identified associations within several sociodemographic subgroups. Two-adult household residence was consistently associated with better HRQoL. Single-adult household status may represent a simple social risk marker to inform survivorship assessment.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancers (TNBCs) are associated with poor prognosis and chemoresistance. Recent reports indicate that extracellular matrix (ECM) molecules, such as integrins, could influence TNBC development. Integrins are adhesion macromolecules that modulate ECM characteristics such as stiffening of ECM and being associated with hypoxia. Therefore, dysregulation in integrins could compromise the efficient delivery of cancer treatments. Some peptides and aptamers can directly target integrins, and they are now being studied; however, most monoclonal antibodies and PARP inhibitors that are used for TNBC do not directly target integrins. Integrins and the ECM can change the way these treatments work. Currently, the efficacy of these candidates is still being evaluated, and the majority of studies are in the early phase of development. The present article reviews the role of integrins in cancer development and captures the state-of-the-art evidence on the therapeutic targeting of integrins in breast cancer. Also, solutions to overcome challenges in the field are suggested.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore the correlation between the ability of M2-type tumor-correlated macrophage-derived exosomes (EXOs) to trigger the aggressiveness of gastric cancer (GC) cells and the miR-132-3p expression. EXOs were isolated from the conditioned media of M0 and M2 macrophages and characterized by transmission electron microscopy and Western blotting. miR-132-3p expression was determined by qRT-PCR. HGC-27 cells were divided into the control, miR-132-3p mimic, miR-132-3p inhibitor, M0-EXO, and M2-EXO groups. Cell viability, proliferation, migration, and invasion were assessed using CCK-8, EdU, and Transwell assays. Intracellular GSH, SOD, MDA, and iron levels were measured using colorimetric assays. FTH1, LIFR, and GPX4 expressions were detected by Western blotting. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were performed to investigate miR-132-3p-mediated transcriptional changes and ferroptosis-related pathways in HGC-27 cells. miR-132-3p was significantly enriched in M2 macrophage-derived exosomes and was highly expressed in GC, with its expression associated with tumor stage, grade, and other clinicopathological features. M2-Exo treatment significantly increased miR-132-3p levels in HGC-27 cells. Both miR-132-3p overexpression and M2-Exo treatment enhanced the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HGC-27 cells, and were accompanied by reduced intracellular iron and MDA levels, increased GSH content and SOD activity, upregulated FTH1 and GPX4 expression, and decreased LIFR expression. In contrast, miR-132-3p inhibition produced largely opposite effects. RNA-seq identified 275 differentially expressed genes following miR-132-3p overexpression, including 216 upregulated and 59 downregulated genes. GO and KEGG analyses revealed significant alterations in biological processes and pathways related to oxygen transport, ATP synthesis, oxidative phosphorylation, thermogenesis, spliceosome function, and endoplasmic reticulum protein processing. Integration of the RNA-seq-derived DEGs with FerrDb identified 12 ferroptosis-related DEGs, including 11 upregulated genes and 1 downregulated gene. qRT-PCR validation showed expression patterns broadly consistent with the RNA-seq results. miR-132-3p expression in the EXOs of M2-type macrophages was significantly elevated, and the EXOs of M2-type macrophages significantly triggered the aggressiveness of GC cells and inhibited ferroptosis in GC cells, which may be resulting from the prevention of ferroptosis through the transport of miR-132-3p; nevertheless, the specific mechanism of action needs to be further elucidated.

papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. Chemotherapy is central to the management of advanced or metastatic disease and is also used in perioperative settings, but outcomes vary substantially. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an inexpensive and readily available marker of systemic inflammation; its prognostic association in chemotherapy-treated CRC warrants focused evaluation. This study adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to July 15, 2025. Studies evaluating pretreatment NLR in relation to overall survival (OS) or a secondary progression- or recurrence-related time-to-event outcome, including progression-free survival (PFS), disease-free survival (DFS), or recurrence-free survival (RFS), in chemotherapy-treated CRC patients were eligible. Study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were independently conducted by two reviewers. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Thirty-eight studies (41 cohorts; 11,346 patients) were included. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.54-1.84; P < 0.0001) and poorer progression- or recurrence-related survival (HR = 1.61, 95% CI 1.43-1.81; P < 0.0001). The direction of association was generally consistent across exploratory subgroups defined by treatment category, age, geographic region, and NLR cut-off. Leave-one-out analyses did not identify a single study that changed the direction of either pooled association. Between-study heterogeneity and evidence of small-study effects warrant cautious interpretation. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer survival outcomes in chemotherapy-treated CRC. NLR may be a readily available prognostic biomarker, but heterogeneous populations, variable outcome definitions and cut-off values, inconsistent covariate adjustment, and possible small-study effects currently limit its use for clinical decision-making. Prospective validation and methodological standardization are required before routine application. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251136904.

papers.abstract: Mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is uncommon in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP-NETs), yet it represents a critical biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) eligibility. Treatment-associated reduction or loss of MMR protein expression, often without corresponding MSI-H, has been reported in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but comparable changes have not been described in neuroendocrine tumours. Persistent discordance between immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based MMR protein assessment and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an emerging and clinically challenging phenomenon. We report a 55-year-old woman initially diagnosed with rectal NET Grade 1 on endoscopic biopsy; the tumour was upgraded to NET Grade 2 (Ki-67 approximately 20%) on the surgical resectionk specimen. Hepatic metastases were confirmed four months after resection. The first liver biopsy (January 16, 2026) demonstrated partial MMR protein loss by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2+, MSH6-, PMS2-), while concurrent NGS showed microsatellite stability (MSS) and a tumour mutational burden (TMB) of <1 mut/Mb. The patient received two cycles of surufatinib 250 mg orally once daily combined with intravenous carboplatin (500 mg, day 1) and etoposide (160 mg, days 1-3). Restaging CT demonstrated disease progression. A repeat liver biopsy (March 17, 2026) revealed complete loss of all four MMR proteins by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2-, MSH6-, PMS2-), while NGS again confirmed MSS and TMB <1 mut/Mb. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of apparent progressive complete MMR protein loss in the context of sequential platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal NET Grade 2, with persistent IHC-NGS discordance throughout. These findings raise an important question regarding how IHC-defined dMMR should be interpreted in the absence of NGS-confirmed MSI-H, and highlight the complexity of immunotherapy eligibility decisions in rare tumour types. Prospective data are needed to guide clinical practice.

papers.abstract: Ginsenoside Rb2 has demonstrated antitumor activity in multiple malignancies, yet its role in cervical cancer and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. This study investigated the effects of Rb2 on cervical cancer progression and explored whether metabolic reprogramming contributes to PD-L1 regulation. Cell proliferation, migration, invasion, glycolytic activity, lactate production, histone lactylation, and PD-L1 expression were evaluated in cervical cancer cells using CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell, Seahorse analysis, RT-qPCR, western blotting, flow cytometry, and ChIP-qPCR. LDHA regulation was examined by protein and mRNA stability assays, pharmacological inhibition, lysosome immunoprecipitation, gain- and loss-of-function studies, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, and biotinylated Rb2 pull-down assays. T-cell function was assessed by Jurkat T-cell-tumor cell co-culture and IL-2 ELISA. Xenograft models and clinical samples were used for validation. Rb2 significantly inhibited cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth, reducing HeLa and SiHa cell viability by approximately 23.4% and 25.7%, respectively. Rb2 selectively downregulated PD-L1 and suppressed glycolysis and lactate production, with reduced H3K18la/H4K12la lactylation at the PD-L1 promoter. LDHA was the primary glycolytic enzyme reduced by Rb2, without changes in its mRNA. Rb2 decreased LDHA protein stability and promoted its autophagy-lysosome-dependent degradation, with p62 required and the p62-LDHA interaction enhanced by Rb2. Rb2-pretreated tumor cells restored IL-2 production by co-cultured Jurkat T cells, whereas LDHA overexpression reversed this effect. LDHA overexpression partially rescued Rb2's effects, and LDHA correlated positively with PD-L1 in cervical cancer tissues. Rb2 suppresses cervical cancer progression by promoting p62-dependent autophagic degradation of LDHA, thereby inhibiting glycolysis-associated H3K18la and PD-L1 transcription. These findings reveal a p62/LDHA/H3K18la/PD-L1 signaling axis through which Rb2 exerts its antitumor effects.

papers.abstract: Midbody remnants (MBRs), once considered inert cytokinetic debris, are now recognized as architecturally specialized, translationally active organelles whose functions reflect the mode of cell division. This review compares MBR biology in symmetric somatic mitosis and asymmetric oocyte meiosis. In somatic cells, MBRs can be retained or secreted as large extracellular vesicles that carry midbody proteins, RNAs, and translation machinery; their enrichment in stem and cancer cells implicates them in cell-state regulation and identifies them as promising, though unvalidated, substrates for liquid-biopsy biomarkers and therapeutic targeting. In oocytes, meiotic midbodies form a distinctive ring-cap architecture that concentrates local translation and restricts maternal products to the egg, thereby supporting developmental competence. Together, these studies establish division mode as a key determinant of midbody architecture, cargo, fate, and translational potential, linking cytokinesis to cancer biology and reproductive medicine.

papers.abstract: Attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a medical condition that is present in approximately 2.5% of adults worldwide and manifests in a variety of different ways across the lifespan. Adults with ADHD often have coexisting psychiatric disorders such as anxiety, mood, sleep, substance use, and personality disorders and are at increased risk for coexisting somatic conditions such as obesity, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and immune and inflammatory conditions. Hence, such adults may be seen by clinicians providing care for a wide range of psychiatric and somatic conditions. Nevertheless, ADHD remains unrecognized and undiagnosed in many persons. Assessment requires interviewing of the patient for core ADHD symptoms, coexisting conditions, and their functional effects, which can be facilitated by using standardized rating scales. Key components of treatment are psychoeducation and psychostimulant or nonstimulant medication, mostly in combination with psychosocial interventions and lifestyle guidance.

papers.abstract: Recent evidence implicates a metabolic switch in afferent spinal circuits as a key driver of the transition from acute pain– to chronic pain–related behaviors in mice after tissue injury, yet the cellular substrates and functional consequences remain incompletely defined. Using a combination of pharmacological and genetic approaches, we investigated whether metabolic reprogramming in spinal cord cell populations constitutes a causal mechanism linking peripheral injury to the progression to pain chronicity. After peripheral injury induced by a hindpaw formalin injection in mice, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed that spinal oligodendrocytes down-regulated transcripts for myelin protein synthesis and up-regulated transcripts important for lipid biosynthesis. Comparative lipidomics showed that this resource reallocation after peripheral injury was associated with disrupted spinal myelin composition. Moreover, axonal integrity was compromised, causing neuronal accumulation of amyloid precursor protein, enhanced β-site amyloid precursor protein–cleaving enzyme 1 (BACE1) expression, and increased insoluble amyloid-β 42 (Aβ 42 ) during a critical temporal window for the transition to pain chronicity. Blocking Aβ 42 production by BACE1 inhibition or clearing Aβ 42 by intrathecal 4G8 monoclonal antibody injection prevented the emergence of persistent pain after hindpaw formalin injection. Oligodendrocyte-specific deletion of N -acylethanolamine acid amidase, a key regulator of cell metabolism and pain, prevented Aβ 42 release and chronic pain development induced by formalin injection or sciatic nerve ligation. These findings uncover an unexpected mechanistic link between chronic pain and amyloid pathology and identify the NAAA→Aβ 42 pathway as a target for disease-modifying intervention.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Primary mitochondrial diseases affect 1 in 4300 livebirths and cause early death or lifelong disability but our understanding of their impact on survival and causes of death is limited. There is conflicting evidence about whether they cause an increased incidence of cancer. We aimed to determine survival, causes of death and risk of developing cancer in people with mitochondrial disease by linking genetic results with routinely collected healthcare data at a national scale. Methods Individuals with mitochondrial diseases were identified in England (population 60.2 million) by National Health Service diagnostic laboratories and Genomics England. A curated cohort was assembled. Individual consent was not required because the National Disease Registration Service has legal permission to collect patient data. We used national datasets to find out the vital status, cause of death and any cancer diagnoses for each individual. Kaplan-Meier survival, Cox regression model and standardised cancer incidence ratio were analysed. Results 1266 unique individuals were identified, with 1164 having a known region in England. Following clinical review, 1107 were included (527 males, 580 females, median age 48 years, age range from infancy to 90 years). 74% had a mitochondrial DNA diagnosis and 26% had nuclear genetic diagnosis. 170 were deceased. 159 were diagnosed during childhood (14.3%). Most childhood deaths were due to the underlying mitochondrial disorder. Common causes of death in adults included cardiac, cancers, and pneumonia. Survival after diagnosis varied by genetic diagnosis and by age at diagnosis with poorer survival for people diagnosed during childhood (hazard ratio 2.11, p < 0.001) or older age (2.83, p < 0.001) and those with recessive POLG disease (hazard ratio 3.06, p < 0.001). For the whole cohort, survival at 10 years after genetic diagnosis was 80.3% (95% confidence interval 76.9% to 83.7%) and survival at 20 years after diagnosis was 58.9% (95% confidence interval 49.6% to 70.0%). Standardised cancer incidence ratios did not show a difference in cancer incidence compared to the general population. Conclusions Survival was much longer than anticipated, with differences due to the precise genetic diagnosis and age at onset. Despite prior contradictory evidence, there was no increased cancer risk in this large cohort.

papers.abstract: Acute pain management is shifting away from traditional paternalistic models towards more collaborative, patient-centred approaches that emphasise shared decision making and the use of digital health technologies. Here, we review recent advances in digital health technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) that support shared decision making, including interactive decision aids, video narratives, and AI-assisted tools. These innovations have the potential to optimise analgesia, reduce the risks associated with opioids and opioid-related harms, and enhance patient autonomy across surgical, emergency, and primary care settings. Although emerging evidence shows promise in improving prescribing efficiency and increasing patient satisfaction, there are still significant barriers to implementation. These include resource limitations, challenges in selecting appropriate tools, and the necessity for robust validation of AI systems. Herein, we critically evaluate the current evidence, discuss practical strategies for implementation, and provide recommendations for integrating these technologies into routine clinical practice.

papers.abstract: To compare the prognostic performance of the preoperative C-reactive protein to albumin ratio (CAR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index, pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score for predicting mortality after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and to determine whether these biomarkers provide incremental prognostic value beyond European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II. Retrospective observational cohort study. Single-center tertiary training and research hospital. Six hundred eighteen consecutive adults undergoing isolated CABG between January 1, 2022, and December 1, 2024, with complete 1-year follow-up. None. The primary outcomes were intensive care unit mortality rate (11.8%) and 1-year all-cause mortality rate (16.2%). Among all evaluated biomarkers, CAR demonstrated the strongest prognostic performance for both outcomes and independently predicted in-hospital and 1-year mortality after adjustment for EuroSCORE II and base excess. Incorporating CAR into EuroSCORE II improved discrimination and showed favorable internally validated calibration and decision-curve net benefit within the proposed perioperative management framework, whereas the remaining inflammatory indices provided little or no incremental prognostic information. Cell count-based indices, including SII and PIV, did not demonstrate meaningful prognostic discrimination or independent associations with the evaluated mortality outcomes in the present cohort. The optimal CAR threshold was derived and evaluated within the same cohort and should therefore be considered exploratory pending external validation. Preoperative CAR was independently associated with both in-hospital and 1-year mortality after isolated CABG and provided incremental prognostic information beyond EuroSCORE II in the present cohort. Rather than replacing EuroSCORE II, it provides complementary prognostic information by capturing inflammatory and nutritional dimensions not represented in conventional surgical risk models. External multicenter validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Patients with obesity are at an increased risk of postoperative pulmonary complications and impaired lung function after general anaesthesia. Although higher levels of PEEP combined with recruitment manoeuvres may improve intraoperative respiratory mechanics, their effect on postoperative lung function remains uncertain. We evaluated whether high PEEP with recruitment manoeuvres improves postoperative spirometry in obese patients undergoing abdominal surgery. This single-centre substudy of the Protective Ventilation in Obese Patients randomised controlled trial was conducted at Ghent University Hospital, Belgium. Adults with a BMI of ≥35 kg·m-2 undergoing abdominal surgery were randomised to high PEEP (12 cm H2O) with recruitment manoeuvres or low PEEP (4 cm H2O) without routine recruitment manoeuvres. Both groups received low tidal volume ventilation (7 mL·kg-1 predicted body weight). The primary outcome was the change in forced expiratory volume in 1 s (FEV1) from baseline to postoperative day 1. Secondary outcomes included changes in spirometry variables and oxygen saturation. Postoperative spirometry data were available for 44 patients (23 low PEEP, 21 high PEEP). Postoperative lung function declined in all patients. The change in FEV1 from baseline to postoperative day 1 did not differ between the low- and high-PEEP groups (-0.90 [0.68] L vs -0.93 [0.66] L; between-group effect 0.0 L; 95% confidence interval -0.4 to 0.4 L; P=0.89). No differences were observed in secondary outcomes. In obese patients undergoing abdominal surgery with low tidal volume ventilation, high PEEP with recruitment manoeuvers did not improve postoperative spirometric outcomes or oxygen saturation compared with low PEEP without routine recruitment manoeuvres. ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02148692.

papers.abstract: Postoperative pain after open cardiac surgery arises from both sternotomy and chest drains and is often inadequately controlled by anatomically limited techniques. This study compared the serratus posterior superior intercostal plane block (SPSIPB, C3-T10 spread) with superficial parasternal intercostal plane block (PSIPB) plus chest drain-site infiltration. Prospective, randomized, controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment. Single-center tertiary referral cardiac surgery center. Adults undergoing elective open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy; 80 assessed for eligibility, 76 randomized. Bilateral SPSIPB (n = 35) or bilateral PSIPB plus local anesthetic infiltration at mediastinal and pleural chest drain sites (n = 41), performed preoperatively under ultrasound guidance. The primary outcome was cumulative 24-hour opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME); the registered secondary outcomes were Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores at rest and on coughing and the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) at 24 hours. All other comparisons were exploratory. Twelve patients were excluded after randomization (2 SPSIPB, 10 control), leaving 33 and 31 for analysis. Opioid consumption was significantly lower in the SPSIPB group (36.6 ± 17.5 v 56.7 ± 16.1 mg of MME; mean difference 20.1 mg of MME; 95% CI, 11.7-28.5; p < 0.001). NRS scores were comparable during the first postoperative hour but lower in the SPSIPB group from 2 hours onward during coughing and at 4, 8, and 24 hours at rest (all p ≤ 0.019). QoR-15 scores were higher in the SPSIPB group (119 [112-126] v 108 [105-111.5]; median difference 10 points; 95% CI, 6-15; p < 0.001), exceeding the minimal clinically important difference of 6 points. Adverse events, including postoperative nausea and vomiting, did not differ between the groups. Compared with PSIPB plus drain-site infiltration-an active comparator targeting both the sternal and drain regions-SPSIPB reduced opioid consumption and improved quality of recovery and may be a valuable component of multimodal analgesia within Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols.

papers.abstract: To compare high-frequency low-tidal volume (HFLTV) ventilation with standard ventilation (SV) regarding procedural efficiency, airway mechanics, and clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation. Retrospective, observational, nonrandomized cohort study. Electrophysiology laboratory of a single tertiary-care university hospital. There were 160 consecutive eligible adults undergoing first-time AF radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia between June 2023 and May 2024. Patients received HFLTV (n = 80; respiratory rate 25-30 breaths/min, tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg, ETCO₂ maintained <50 mmHg) or SV (n = 80; tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg, respiratory rate 10-12 breaths/min) per attending anesthesiologist practice. All received propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia. Primary outcomes were total procedure time and radiofrequency ablation time; secondary outcomes were airway pressures, oxygenation, AF recurrence at 1 and 6 months, AF-related hospitalization, and complications. HFLTV was associated with lower median procedure time (110 v 128 minutes; p < .001) and ablation time (23 v 28 minutes; p < .001). Peak (14 v 18 cmH₂O) and minimum (13 v 15 cmH₂O) airway pressures were lower with HFLTV (both p < .001), whereas ETCO₂ and SpO₂ nadir were comparable. Multivariable regression identified HFLTV as an independent predictor of shorter ablation time (nonstandardized β=-5.48 minutes; 95% CI -7.05 to -3.91; p < .001). In exploratory analyses, recurrence at 1 month (7.5% v 15.0%; p = .211) and 6 months (13.8% v 18.8%; p = .520) and 6-month AF-related hospitalization (12.5% v 18.8%; p = .384) were numerically lower with HFLTV but confidence intervals were wide and included no difference. In a consecutive cohort including paroxysmal and persistent AF, HFLTV was associated with shorter procedure and ablation times and lower measured airway pressures without compromising gas exchange. Clinical outcome analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, warranting prospective randomized evaluation.

papers.abstract: Intraoperative noise is an occupational hazard with the potential to compromise anaesthetist performance and patient safety. The WHO recommends hospital sound exposure ≤ 35 dB LAeq (A-weighted equivalent continuous sound level), yet noise levels routinely exceed this level. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine intraoperative noise levels worldwide. Five databases were searched from inception to May 2026, in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Studies were eligible for inclusion if they included surgical specialty and a measure of noise sampled recorded with validated sound metres. Studies were eligible for meta-analysis if they included a mean time-weighted average. Two authors undertook searches and risk-of-bias assessment. Meta-regression estimated pooled means, heterogeneity, and variance. Fifty studies met the inclusion criteria in the systematic review, with 28 studies providing 43 unique datasets subclassified by type of surgical procedure for analysis. The pooled random-effects mean intraoperative noise level was 70.7 A-weighted dB [dB(A)] (95% CI 69.0-72.3). Subgroup analysis demonstrated the highest exposures in otolaryngology at 78.8 dB(A) (95% CI 72.8-84.7) and orthopaedics at 73.3 dB(A) (95% CI 68.9-77.8). Meta-regression confirmed surgical specialty as a significant predictor of mean exposure (Q=25.8, degrees of freedom=6, P=0.0002). Anaesthetists are consistently exposed to intraoperative sound levels exceeding WHO guidelines, particularly in high-intensity specialties such as orthopaedics and otolaryngology. These findings provide a specialty-specific synthesis of noise exposure and highlight the need for targeted interventions, standardised measurement, and research linking exposure to clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract: Simulation-based interdisciplinary training improves perinatal outcomes, but scalable and adaptable models for diverse labor and delivery (L&D) settings remain limited. The TeaM-L&DSim (Interdisciplinary Training for Patient Safety and Quality Care in Modern Labor & Delivery Simulation) program was developed by the No Pain Labor & Delivery-Global Health Initiative, combining nontechnical and technical simulation training, to enhance team functions, clinical decision-making, emergency preparedness, and complex care in resource-variable maternity care environments. We implemented TeaM-L&DSim using a mixed-methods quality improvement framework nationally at six training hubs in the first year, with obstetricians, anesthesiologists, neonatologists, midwives/nurses, and hospital administrators from 52 hospitals in China. The program emphasized three educational innovations: the Three Co(re) Domains (Collaboration, Cognition, and Competence), the 4P Strategy (Prevision, Prophylaxis, Preparedness, Prompt responses), and a cascading mentorship model for trainer development. Training included 27 standardized simulation modules delivered through hybrid virtual-physical formats. Evaluation was structured using the four levels of the Kirkpatrick model (reaction, learning, behavior, and results). Data sources included pre/post-training surveys, voluntary feedback, site-level implementation audits, and observational reports. Ninety-seven percent of participants reported that the training met or exceeded expectations. Self-reported outcomes included improved interdisciplinary communication (92.7%), greater emergency response confidence (88.2%), and clearer role understanding (90.5%). A one-year follow-up survey with 29% response rate indicated 72% of respondents reported changes in personal practice, while 43% reported institution-initiated protocol modifications. These changes saw greater impact in Level 3A hospitals. The program demonstrated feasibility across both urban academic and rural hospitals, with early reports noting enhanced team dynamics and emergency response times. TeaM-L&DSim is a scalable, interdisciplinary simulation program that improved team-based clinical competencies in L&D units, better effective in Level 3A facilities. More data are needed to understand adaptation to lower resource settings. This model holds promise for broader dissemination in global maternal safety initiatives.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way we discover anticancer drugs. It tackles the problems of traditional methods, such as prolonged timelines for drug development, higher costs, and substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. This review explains how AI is applied throughout the cancer drug pipeline. This includes target identification, virtual screening of compounds, molecular docking, and predicting pharmacokinetics. We explore how machine learning models speed up hit-to-lead optimization, improve clinical trial design by stratifying patients, and allow for real-time toxicity monitoring. A key focus is on integrating AI with multi-omics data, including proteomics, genomics, transcriptomics, and metabolomics, to support precision oncology and personalized treatments. We address important validation challenges, like model interpretability, data quality, and regulatory issues that must be solved before AI can be widely used in clinics. By summarizing current evidence and targeting research gaps, this review offers a clear view of how AI is enhancing the discovery, personalization, and validation of anticancer treatments.

papers.abstract: Adverse neurocognitive and functional outcomes are common after cardiac surgery. Cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitors regional cerebral oxygen saturation, allowing clinicians to detect and reverse cerebral desaturation. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs to evaluate whether intraoperative NIRS monitoring improves neurocognitive outcomes after cardiac surgery. We searched CENTRAL, CINAHL, Embase, MEDLINE, PsycINFO, and Web of Science for RCTs comparing NIRS-guided intraoperative management with usual care in adults undergoing on-pump cardiac surgery, assessing the outcomes of postoperative cognitive decline, delirium, stroke, mortality, and functional recovery. We pooled data using random-effects meta-analysis and assessed certainty of evidence using GRADE methodology. We included 17 RCTs (N=2288). NIRS-guided management probably reduces early postoperative cognitive decline (risk ratio [RR] 0.65, 95% CI 0.42-0.99; I2=65%, moderate certainty), may have little or no effect on stroke (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.42-1.91; low certainty) or mortality (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.47-1.52; low certainty), and may have no effect on delirium (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56-1.09; I2=32%, low certainty). Findings were primarily derived from small, single-centre trials with heterogenous NIRS thresholds and intervention algorithms. Few studies evaluated outcomes beyond 30 days, and none evaluated validated measures of quality of life or function. Although NIRS-guided intraoperative care shows promise for reducing early postoperative cognitive decline after cardiac surgery, evidence of benefit for other neurocognitive or clinical outcomes remains limited. Large multicentre studies are needed to confirm its utility, refine intervention thresholds, and determine its impact on long-term cognition, function, and quality of life. Systematic review protocol. PROSPERO (CRD42022336468).

papers.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) has been increasingly linked to postoperative complications and adverse outcomes. Nevertheless, the association between preoperative hemoglobin levels and the risk of IOH has not been investigated. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 2,060 patients aged ≥ 18 yr who underwent general anesthesia between 2019 and 2023. We defined intraoperative hypotension as any mean blood pressure (MBP) < 65, 60, 55, 50, or 45 mm Hg, based on 5-min interval recordings. We assessed the association between preoperative hemoglobin levels and IOH using multivariable logistic regression with restricted cubic spline modeling. We also evaluated the association between preoperative hemoglobin levels and postoperative length of hospital stay using a generalized additive model. We found no significant association between preoperative hemoglobin levels and IOH risk at MBP < 65 and < 45 mm Hg (P = 0.13 and 0.12, respectively). Nevertheless, at MBP < 60 mm Hg, patients with lower preoperative hemoglobin levels had a significantly higher risk of IOH (P = 0.03). We observed similar trends at more severe hypotension thresholds (< 55 mm Hg and < 50 mm Hg), with P values of 0.02 and 0.03, respectively. Lower hemoglobin levels were associated with more frequent IOH episodes and higher odds ratios. We also found a significant association between lower preoperative hemoglobin levels and a longer postoperative length of hospital stay. Lower preoperative hemoglobin levels were significantly associated with an increased risk of IOH and longer postoperative length of hospital stay. These findings highlight the potential value of incorporating hemoglobin level assessments into IOH risk stratification and may help improve patient outcomes.

papers.abstract: This technical note is meant to be complementary to the recently published Professional Practice Guidelines of the SFAR-ADARPEF. The limits of using blood pressure as a surrogate for changes in cardiac output and the variable accuracy of its non-invasive measurement are reminded. As clearcut population-based threshold values based on measurements obtained in awake or anaesthetised children cannot be provided, an adaptation based on the child's baseline blood pressure, comorbidity and surgical context is necessary to prevent unnecessary treatment of an acceptable low blood pressure or tolerating a too low blood pressure. The measurement of a baseline awake blood pressure, although often difficult to achieve in children, is therefore very helpful. If a low intraoperative MAP is measured, the presence of hypotension should be confirmed by repeat measurement and the simultaneous evaluation of clinical and paraclinical signs, and the observation of the surgical field. The treatment should then be adapted to the cause: anaesthetic overdose, hypovolaemia, positioning, surgical action, anaphylaxis, etc.

papers.abstract: Women with cardiogenic shock (CS) under VA-ECMO face excess mortality, yet the pharmacological basis of this disparity remains poorly understood. Arginine vasopressin (AVP) is increasingly used as a non-adrenergic vasopressor in this setting, but whether sex modifies the hemodynamic response to AVP is unknown. In this multicenter retrospective cohort of VA-ECMO-supported CS patients, we assessed whether sex was independently associated with successful vasopressor de-escalation at 48 hours (norepinephrine equivalent dose [NEE] <0.25 µg/kg/min) after AVP initiation. Multivariable logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to evaluate sex differences in treatment response and NEE trajectories over time. Among 193 eligible patients, 32% of women achieved successful de-escalation versus 49% of men (p = 0.023). Male sex was independently associated with treatment success (aOR 2.08, 95% CI 1.07-4.15, p = 0.033). A significant sex-by-time interaction was observed in NEE trajectories (p = 0.041), with divergence emerging at 48 hours (NEE 0.24 vs. 0.01 µg/kg/min, p = 0.008). The excess failure risk was confined to postmenopausal women aged ≥55 years (aOR 2.75, 95% CI 1.32-5.93, p = 0.008). Female sex, particularly in a postmenopausal context, was independently associated with impaired vasopressor de-escalation following AVP in CS on VA-ECMO. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that hormonal status may modulate vascular responsiveness to AVP and support the need for prospective studies incorporating hormonal profiling.

papers.abstract: Apnea testing is mandatory for brain death determination but may induce hypoxemia despite standard preoxygenation procedures. High-flow oxygen (HFO) systems may improve apneic oxygenation during the procedure, although clinical data remain limited. We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study including consecutive adult patients undergoing apnea testing for brain death determination between January 2023 and May 2026. Standard oxygen insufflation (6-15 L/min) was compared with HFO delivered through the Opt970® interface (Fisher & Paykel) at 50 L/min and FiO2 1.0. The primary outcome was longitudinal pulse oximetry saturation (SpO2) evolution during apnea testing. Secondary outcomes included desaturation events and arterial blood gas parameters. Repeated SpO2 measurements were analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model. A total of 144 apnea tests were analyzed, including 78 using standard oxygen insufflation and 66 using HFO. Baseline characteristics and ventilatory parameters were comparable between groups. Lowest SpO2 during apnea testing was significantly higher with HFO (100 [98-100] vs. 99 [95-99]; p = 0.003), while desaturation below 94% occurred less frequently (9.1% vs. 21.8%; p = 0.04). Post-test PaCO2 was slightly higher in the HFO group (73 [67-81] vs. 70 [62-77] mmHg; p = 0.04). Longitudinal mixed-effects analysis demonstrated a significant decrease in SpO2 over time in both groups (p < 0.0001). However, HFO was associated with overall higher SpO2 values throughout the procedure (β=+1.38; standard error 0.69; p = 0.047), without significant group-by-time interaction (p = 0.578). HFO delivered through the Opt970® device was associated with modestly higher oxygen saturation during apnea testing compared with standard oxygen insufflation. Further prospective studies are required to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract: Data are lacking regarding current ventilatory settings during abdominal surgery. Expert recommendations emphasize the need for protective ventilation, and several tools are now available to individualize positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP). We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey among French anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists in November 2025 to assess ventilatory settings during abdominal surgery, both for laparotomy and laparoscopy. Protective ventilation was defined as the combination of low tidal volume (6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight), low-to-moderate PEEP (5-8 cm H2O), and recruitment maneuvers. Individualization of PEEP was defined as the use of driving pressure, mechanical power, or compliance to titrate PEEP. Among 1091 anesthesiologists and nurse anesthetists, female responders accounted for 46% (497/1084), the median age of anesthesia providers was 39 (33-47) years, and most responders (77%, 839/1090) had an adult-based main field of activity. Main ventilatory settings used during laparotomy were 6 to 8 ml/kg of predicted body weight (93%, 1013/1084), a respiratory rate set according to EtCO2 in 53% of responders (579/1084), and a PEEP set between 5 and 8 cmH20 for 87% of responders (950/1091). Most participants performed recruitment maneuvers (98%, 1065/1091). Overall, protective ventilation was used in 70% (763/1090), and individualization of PEEP in 45% (479/1054). Similar ventilatory settings were reported for laparoscopy. In this nationwide survey, expert consensus-based recommendations for protective ventilation during abdominal surgery appeared widely implemented in France. In contrast, individualized PEEP strategies were reported in fewer than half of cases, reflecting ongoing uncertainty and variability regarding PEEP titration in routine perioperative practice.

papers.abstract: Anesthesiologists play a central role in optimizing perioperative care and improving outcomes for patients with hip fractures (HF). Standardized care bundles are essential to guide clinicians, enhance expertise, and improve overall quality of care. We conducted a nationwide modified Delphi study to establish French expert consensus on key components of a standardized care bundle for patients over 75 years old with HF. A two-round modified Delphi process was conducted with 30 multidisciplinary experts representative of major French academic societies to assess consensus on perioperative care practices for HF in patients over 75. Experts rated 34 clinically relevant items using a 9-point Likert scale, with consensus defined as ≥70% rating ranging from 7 to 9 for agreement or 1 to 3 for disagreement. The process was conducted via the REDCap platform and adhered to ethical and data protection standards. The expert panel included 11 (36.7%) anesthesiologists, 9 (30%) geriatricians, 6 (20%) orthopedic surgeons, and 4 (13.3%) hospital pharmacists. Agreement consensus was reached for 29 out of 34 proposed items. A shortlist of 12 items that achieved over 90% consensus was identified, comprising 2 organizational, 7 perioperative, and 3 surgical items. The bundle of care for HF elaborated in this study provides perioperative teams with clear, actionable objectives to improve care quality and equity. Its impact on patient outcomes warrants further evaluation.

papers.abstract: Induction of anesthesia is one of the most distressing moments for pediatric patients during their perioperative experience. They may consequently refuse induction at the last minute. Anesthesia providers are then placed in a challenging ethical dilemma: they must seek to gain the child's cooperation, force the child to undergo induction using restraint, or delay the case. In the moment, it can be difficult to parse the relevant clinical and ethical factors to determine the most appropriate course of action. The purpose of this perspective paper is to provide a clinical ethics framework to support anesthesia provider decision making during instances of last-minute pediatric refusal of anesthesia induction. Three prominent pediatric ethics concepts support this framework, including the harm principle, best interests, and emerging autonomy. This framework uses the criteria of (1) urgency of intervention, (2) decision-making ability of the patient, and (3) harms to the patient from a forced induction. Each of these criteria is discussed in depth as it relates to last-minute pediatric refusal. Case illustrations are provided to demonstrate the clinical utility of this framework in everyday practice.

papers.abstract: In-hospital diabetes mellitus management currently relies on intermittent glucose monitoring with point-of-care (POC) testing, rather than continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Most studies on CGM have focused on its benefits and accuracy in the outpatient setting, in contrast to the hospital setting, where the accuracy may be different. In this prospective observational study (NCT06297850), we assessed the accuracy of CGM (Dexcom G7, Dexcom Inc.) compared with POC monitors in people with diabetes mellitus requiring glucose-lowering medication undergoing surgery or admission to the ICU. The primary outcome was agreement between CGM and POC measurements, defined as median absolute relative difference (MARD). Clarke error grid (CEG) and Bland-Altman analyses were used to quantify the accuracy. Secondary analyses assessed agreement during periods of hypoperfusion, defined as a mean arterial pressure of <65 mm Hg, infusions with vasopressors, or reduced peripheral perfusion index. In 58 participants (mean [standard deviation] age 71 [11]yr; 34% female), the median MARD was 10.9% (5.1-19.4%); 1186 of 1212 paired POC and CGM measurements (98%) were within clinically acceptable ranges (CEG zones A and B). MARD was 4.5% higher (95% confidence interval 2.3-6.7%) during periods of hypoperfusion. Given that hypoglycaemia (<4 mM) did not occur, no paired readings were obtained. Bland-Altman analysis showed similar CGM and POC measurements, with a mean difference of -1 mM (95% limits of agreement -5.6 to 3.4 mM). For the vast majority of interstitial glucose measurements, CGM was accurate in people with diabetes mellitus. Although overall performance was good, caution may be warranted when interpreting CGM data during periods of impaired peripheral perfusion. NCT06297850.

papers.abstract: Increasing numbers of patients aged ≥ 90 years require elective surgery. Frailty is increasingly recognised as a key determinant of peri-operative risk, but high-quality evidence to understand the impact on outcomes in this age group is limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Australian and New Zealand Intensive Care Society Adult Patient Database. Patients aged ≥ 90 years admitted to ICU following elective surgery were included, encompassing planned and unplanned ICU admissions. Frailty was assessed at ICU admission using the Clinical Frailty Scale and patients categorised as non-frail or frail. Propensity score matching was performed to balance age; sex; acute illness severity; and comorbidities. Primary outcome was 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU mortality; in-hospital mortality; return to pre-admission residence; and ICU and duration of hospital stay. The matched cohort comprised 5398 patients (2699 without frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 1-4) and 2699 living with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 5-8)), with good post-matching covariate balance. Mortality in ICU was low and not significantly different between patients who were frail and non-frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (matched hazard ratio (HR) 1.66, 95%CI 1.22-2.27, p = 0.001) and higher 1-year mortality (matched HR 1.66, 95%CI 1.47-1.87, p < 0.001). Patients without frailty had higher odds of returning to their pre-admission residence at hospital discharge than patients living with frailty (matched OR 1.45, 95%CI 1.29-1.62, p < 0.001). Patients who were frail experienced longer hospital stays and higher rates of postoperative complications, including delirium and acute renal failure. Among patients aged ≥ 90 years undergoing elective surgery with postoperative intensive care admission, frailty is strongly associated with prolonged recovery and worse short and long-term outcomes. Incorporation of frailty assessment into peri-operative pathways may improve risk stratification, shared decision-making and personalised care for patients aged ≥ 90 years.

papers.abstract: Although carbon dioxide (CO2) is widely regarded as a driver for cerebral vasomodulation, often termed cerebrovascular CO2-reactivity, experimental evidence has shown that this response is primarily mediated through changes in pH rather than CO2. This complicates the management of cerebral blood flow (CBF) during the treatment of acid-base disorders with partial respiratory or metabolic compensation, when the CBF has normalized together with pH equilibration, despite persistent hyper- or hypercapnia. Although a pH-guided approach would therefore be preferred, no quantitative estimate of the relationship between pH and CBF has currently been reported in the literature. Therefore, this study aims to estimate the cerebrovascular sensitivity to pH and explore whether changes in CBF velocity (CBFV) are more closely related to arterial pH or CO2. In patients undergoing cardiac surgery, CBFV and continuous in-line arterial blood gas monitoring, incorporated in the cardiopulmonary bypass circuit, were analyzed. Mixed-effects models were constructed with percentage change in CBFV as response variable and arterial pH and/or CO2 as explanatory variable(s). Model fit of the explanatory variables was compared using marginal and conditional R2. Improvement of model fit and parsimony were assessed with the likelihood-ratio test (LRT) and change in Akaike information criterion (ΔAIC), respectively. Thirteen patients were included in the analysis with a total of 1960 datapoints. CBFV decreased by 30.6% per 0.1 increase in arterial pH (95% confidence interval [CI], 28.9-32.2; P < .0001), and increased by 1.95% per mm Hg increase in PaCO2 (95% CI, 1.76-2.14; P < .0001). Arterial pH explained a greater proportion of variance than PaCO2 (marginal R2: 0.444 vs 0.294; conditional R2: 0.744 vs 0.530). Furthermore, adding arterial pH to the null CO2-model considerably improved model fit (LRT = 616.4) and parsimony (ΔAIC = -615), whereas adding arterial CO2 to the pH-model barely improved model fit (LRT = 4.6) and parsimony (ΔAIC = -3). This exploratory study provides a quantitative estimate of the relationship between CBFV and pH, and suggests that changes in CBFV are more closely related to arterial pH than to CO2. This estimate of the cerebrovascular sensitivity to pH was used to describe a feasible pH-guided approach in the management of CBF during the treatment of partially compensated acid-base disorders.

papers.abstract: The Risk Assessment of Morbidity in Pediatric Surgery (RAMPS) score was developed by a tertiary care children's center to predict risk of noncardiac pediatric surgical morbidity using intrinsic surgical risk (ISR) and individual comorbidity. The score demonstrated good internal validity, discrimination, and generalizability. This study seeks to externally validate the score in a similar patient population at a different tertiary care children's hospital. Following institutional review board (IRB) approval, data for all noncardiac, nontrauma, and nontransplant pediatric surgeries performed at the external children's hospital in 2019 were collected via review of medical records. The RAMPS score for each patient was calculated. A composite morbidity score defined as transfer to intensive care unit (ICU), cardiac arrest, unplanned endotracheal intubation, or unplanned initiation of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) in the 72 hours following surgery was calculated. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and calibration between predicted and observed risk of morbidity was assessed. Of 13,718 patients included, 409 (2.98%) experienced the composite morbidity outcome. The most common morbidity was postoperative PPV-361 (2.63%). Only 1.5% (n = 205) of the cohort was critically ill, though 14.1% (n = 1934) had at least three chronic conditions and 19.5% (n = 2668) of patients had a procedure in ISR quartiles 3 or 4. Each component of the RAMPS score was significantly associated with the outcome. The RAMPS score had very good discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.829; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.809-0.849) and good calibration between observed and predicted probabilities (Brier score = 0.03). The RAMPS score performed well in this external validation with overall less patient complexity and less morbidity than in the original cohort included for development and internal validation. The score moderately overestimated risk in the most complex patients, which does not diminish its utility in guiding resource allocation to manage or prevent perioperative adverse events. In summary, the RAMPs score is a simple, highly discriminant, well-calibrated, and externally validated tool clinicians and health systems can use to predict morbidity among pediatric surgery patients.

papers.abstract: While antiretroviral therapy has improved surgical safety for people living with HIV, comprehensive data on perioperative organ injury and its impact on patient safety remain limited. This study aimed to compare the incidence of perioperative organ injury, in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay, and hospitalization costs between people living with HIV and HIV-negative individuals undergoing surgery in the United States. This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2021. The population-based sample included adult patients (age >18 years) identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. Of 41,622,004 eligible surgical admissions, 2,088,307 (5.0%) were people living with HIV and 39,533,697 were HIV-negative. Primary outcomes were perioperative organ injury incidence and associated mortality; secondary outcomes included hospital length of stay and total hospital charges. Adjusted models accounted for baseline characteristics and surgical complexity. Among the 41,622,004 surgical admissions, people living with HIV were found to be older and carried a significantly higher comorbidity burden, with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 8 compared to 1 in the HIV-negative group. Perioperative organ injury occurred in 1,348,363 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (64.6%) compared with 7,867,547 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (19.9%). Acute myocardial infarction (33.5%) and acute kidney injury (22.0%) were the most common injuries among people living with HIV. In-hospital mortality occurred in 66,935 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (3.2%) compared with 872,170 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (2.2%). Hospital length of stay and hospital charges were also significantly higher. Adjusted analyses demonstrated that HIV status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-1.78), longer hospital length of stay (β = 2.73 days; 95% CI, 2.56-2.90), a decreased likelihood of home discharge (hazard ratio [HR], 0.73; 95% CI, 0.72-0.73), and increased hospitalization costs (β = $18,423; 95% CI, 16,712-20,134). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that elevated perioperative risk persisted among patients with asymptomatic HIV infection, although the greatest risk was observed among patients with symptomatic HIV disease/AIDS. People living with HIV incur a significantly higher risk of perioperative organ injury and worse surgical outcomes despite advances in antiretroviral therapy. HIV status was independently associated with adverse perioperative outcomes in adjusted models, supporting its inclusion as a risk stratification variable in surgical planning. Future research should incorporate immunologic markers, such as CD4 count and viral load, to further refine perioperative risk prediction and optimize outcomes for this population.
