papers.abstract: The external oblique intercostal (EOI) plane block is a fascial plane block that targets the unilateral cutaneous branches of intercostal nerves, and spares the sympathetic trunk. We hypothesized that the ultrasound-guided EOI plane block might provide superior analgesia compared to systemic analgesia alone for patients after open liver surgery. In this double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 74 patients scheduled for open liver surgery were assigned to receive either EOI plane block with 30 mL of 0.375% ropivacaine (n = 37) or no EOI plane block (n = 37). All patients received postoperative standard patient-controlled intravenous analgesia. Primary outcome was the resting numerical rating scale (NRS) pain score at 3 h postoperatively. The key secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, and the total number of analgesia interventions at 3 h, 6 h, 24 h, 48 h, and 72 h postoperatively; opioid-related side effects and block-related complications; postoperative functional recovery outcomes; total ropivacaine plasma concentrations at 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, and 180 min post-block. The primary outcome, the resting NRS pain score at 3 h postoperatively, was significantly lower in the block group than in the control group. The block group showed a shorter length of hospital stay. There were no significant differences in cumulative opioid consumption, frequency of analgesia, or opioid-related side effects. No block-related complications were observed, and total ropivacaine plasma concentrations remained below the toxicity threshold. Ultrasound-guided EOI plane block reduces early postoperative pain. This technique should be regarded as a safe and effective component within a comprehensive postoperative multimodal analgesia regimen.

papers.abstract: Fibrinogen concentrate (FC) has a well-established safety profile and is recommended for treating acquired fibrinogen deficiency. However, its comparative effectiveness vs other treatments regarding transfusions and patient outcomes remains uncertain. Comparative studies from a range of clinical settings in which patients received FC for acquired hypofibrinogenaemia and that evaluated blood product needs, mortality, thromboembolic events, or hospital length of stay were included in a systematic literature review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO: CRD42024602804). Meta-analyses used pooled data to provide an estimate of the difference in outcome between FC and all other treatments; separate analyses were conducted for adult and paediatric patients. Overall, 58 studies (N=13 530 patients) were analysed. Adult FC recipients received significantly fewer red blood cell, fresh frozen plasma, and platelet units than with other treatments: 28% (incidence rate ratio [IRR] 0.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.59-0.89; P=0.002), 31% (IRR 0.69; 95% CI 0.54-0.89; P=0.004), and 44% less (IRR 0.56; 95% CI 0.33-0.95; P=0.03), respectively. These results were largely driven by cardiac surgery studies. In an RCT subanalysis, the use and quantity of blood products were significantly reduced with FC. No significant difference in mortality or thromboembolic events was found between treatments in adult patients or in any outcomes analysed in paediatric patients. This meta-analysis suggests FC administered for acquired hypofibrinogenaemia can reduce blood product transfusions in adults, with no obvious safety concerns, compared with other treatments.

papers.abstract: Opioid use disorder may increase the risk of adverse postoperative outcomes, but the magnitude and consistency of this association remain unclear. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the impact of opioid use disorder on postoperative outcomes across surgical populations. We searched electronic databases for studies comparing adults (aged ≥ 18 y) with and without opioid use disorder undergoing surgery. Primary outcomes were the incidence of any postoperative pain and composite adverse respiratory outcomes. Secondary outcomes included re-admission rates 30 and 90 days after surgery; in-hospital mortality; duration of hospital stay; and total healthcare costs. From the 40 included studies, three reported postoperative pain, and 19 reported respiratory outcomes. People with opioid use disorder had higher odds of postoperative pain (OR 2.87, 95%CI 1.63-5.06) and composite adverse respiratory events (OR 2.10, 95%CI 1.64-2.68), both with moderate certainty. Subgroup analyses showed increased risk of pulmonary embolism, pneumonia and other respiratory and pulmonary complications (low to moderate certainty). Low certainty evidence indicated higher 30-day and 90-day re-admission rates, prolonged duration of hospitalisation and higher total healthcare costs associated with opioid use disorder, while in-hospital mortality did not differ significantly (very low certainty). Our results suggest that opioid use disorder is associated with higher incidence of postoperative pain, increased postoperative complications and greater total healthcare costs, which supports the need for routine pre-operative screening for opioid use disorder and the application of patient-centred, multidisciplinary peri-operative care and pain management.

papers.abstract: Cancellation on the day of elective surgery is a persistent challenge that compromises operating theatre efficiency, wastes resources and delays patient care. Existing evidence is difficult to interpret because definitions of cancellation vary across studies and reported reasons are classified inconsistently. We aimed to estimate the incidence of cancellation on the day of surgery and synthesise the reported reasons for cancellation. Databases were searched for observational studies reporting elective surgery cancellations. Studies explicitly defining cancellation on the day of surgery were included in a random-effects meta-analysis of proportions. Subgroup analyses examined variation by national income level and surgical speciality, with geographical region explored in supplementary analyses. Included studies were assessed for risk of bias using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Reported reasons were synthesised narratively across four domains: patient; medical/anaesthesia; administrative/system; and surgery/staff. Fifty-eight studies met the eligibility criteria, of which 37 (with a strict definition of on-the-day cancellation of surgery) were included. Pooled incidence of cancellation on the day of surgery was 14% (95%CI 13-16%), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 99.91%). Rates varied by national income level and surgical speciality, with higher estimates reported in low- and lower-middle-income settings and in some specialities, including ophthalmology and neurosurgery. Reasons reported most commonly included: patient declining surgery; non-fasted; unstable medical condition; changes in clinical status; improper scheduling or overbooking; instrument unavailability; and staff shortages. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the findings and no clear publication bias was detected. The certainty of evidence for the pooled incidence estimate was low. Cancellation on the day of surgery remains a substantial and globally relevant peri-operative problem. Its burden and drivers are highly context-dependent and often reflect weaknesses in pre-operative preparation, organisational co-ordination and system capacity. Reducing avoidable cancellations may therefore require context-specific strategies targeting pathway reliability, timely pre-anaesthetic assessment and peri-operative resource alignment.

papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia is a chronic pain disorder frequently co-occurring with depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and insomnia, particularly in veterans, and safer nonpharmacological therapies are needed. Cranial electrotherapy stimulation, also referred to as cranial electrotherapy stimulation (CES), may help with anxiety and sleep, but its effect on pain is unclear. This feasibility study evaluated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to identify neural correlates of pain and treatment response for CES effects on fibromyalgia pain in veterans. In a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial at a single US government hospital, veterans aged 20 to 60 with fibromyalgia were assigned to active or sham in-home CES, stratified by sex. Participants self-administered CES for 60 minutes daily over 12 weeks. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) was acquired at baseline, 6 weeks, and 12 weeks with clinical outcomes, including the Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale (DVPRS), National Institutes of Health (NIH) Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) measures, and tests of physical function. Forty-eight participants were randomized (25 active, 23 sham) and 47 were analyzed. Both groups showed significant improvements in DVPRS pain (-1.88 ± 2.2) and pain interference with sleep (-2.25 ± 2.8), mood (-1.88 ± 2.6), activity (-1.83 ± 2.4) and stress (-1.77 ± 3.0) at 12 weeks versus baseline (P < .01), with significant between-group differences only in sleep (P = .04). Neuroimaging revealed significant increases in connectivity between the cerebellar 7b seed and the left occipital fusiform gyrus (0.079 ± 0.1) left lingual gyrus (0.063 ± 0.08), and right lingual gyrus (0.058 ± 0.08) for the CES group and decreases in the sham group (-0.088 ± 0.1; -0.121 ± 0.08; and -0.135 ± 0.1), respectively. No adverse events occurred. Both groups improved similarly in pain and function, though new analgesic usage was more prevalent in the sham group. Neuroimaging revealed differential changes in cerebellar-sensory-visual networks and baseline patterns distinguishing responders from nonresponders, supporting feasibility and design of larger, adequately powered CES trials in fibromyalgia.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the first-hour arterial-to-end-tidal carbon dioxide gradient as a marker of recorded 90-day mortality, distinguishing association, component interpretation and incremental prediction. Retrospective cohort study. INSPIRE v1.4.2, covering surgery from 2011 to 2020. Adults undergoing their first eligible intracranial operation with arterial carbon dioxide tension (PaCO₂) recorded within 60 min of anesthesia start. End-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO₂) was paired within ±5 min. The outcome was database-recorded all-cause death within 90 days. Firth regression evaluated the gradient without conditioning on either component. The revised principal association model included clinical covariates and contemporaneous mean arterial pressure, heart rate and minute ventilation. Component and internally validated prediction models were secondary. Among 1907 patients, 95 deaths were recorded. The clinical gradient odds ratio (OR) per 5 mmHg was 1.38 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-1.73). The revised principal association model included 1830 patients and 92 events (OR, 1.34; 95% CI, 1.06-1.69). Conditional component estimates did not establish predominance of either component. Adding the gradient to clinical variables, contemporaneous physiology and ETCO₂ changed optimism-corrected area under the curve from 0.832 to 0.833, without improving the Brier score. A larger first-hour gradient was associated with recorded mortality in patients selected for early paired monitoring. Within the evaluated models and metrics, incremental prediction was limited. These findings do not establish a causal mechanism, treatment target or externally validated prediction tool.

papers.abstract: Processed electroencephalogram (pEEG) monitors are commonly used in anesthesia practice. The relationship between the pEEG and clinical levels of sedation over anesthetic concentrations with and without opioids is not well understood. The purpose of this trial was to investigate the relationship between Bispectral IndexTM (BISTM), clinical measures of sedation, and inhaled anesthetics across a range of anesthetic concentrations and hypnotic states with and without intravenous opioids. This prospective, randomized trial enrolled 211 healthy volunteers. Participants were randomized to one of five anesthetic regimens: sevoflurane, sevoflurane with remifentanil, sevoflurane with fentanyl, desflurane, or isoflurane. Target anesthetic end-tidal concentrations were increased in a stepwise fashion until a BIS index of 30 to 40 was reached. Opioids were administered by target-controlled infusion and commenced before the inhaled agent began. At each targeted end-tidal concentration, responsiveness was assessed using the Modified Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) score and the BIS index was recorded. The MOAA/S score was used to assess participant responsiveness, with a score ≤2 considered unresponsive and a score ≥3 considered responsive. The primary outcome measure was the BIS50 for each anesthetic regimen, representing the BIS index at which 50% of participants were unresponsive. Secondary outcomes included BIS95 (representing the BIS index at which 95% of participants were unresponsive) and evaluation of the BIS index as a predictor of responsiveness. BIS50 and BIS95 were estimated using random intercept logistic regression models, and the predictive performance of BIS indices was assessed by calculating the corresponding area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). One hundred and forty-three participants were randomized to a treatment group and completed the procedure with adequate data. Mean age was 26.5 ± 6.7 years (52% male). There were no reported device-related adverse events. Across treatment groups, BIS50 ranged from 67.5 (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.6-71.4) to 76.2 (73.5-78.8), and BIS95 ranged from 49.1 (42.9-55.4) to 63.3 (59.5-67.2). Compared to the sevoflurane and isoflurane groups, the desflurane group exhibited slightly lower BIS50 and BIS95 values. The addition of opioids to sevoflurane had minimal impact on BIS50 and BIS95. The BIS index alone was a strong predictor of the level of responsiveness, with AUCs consistently close to the ideal value of 1 (≥0.95) across all treatment groups. BIS indices were highly correlated with MOAA/S scores. These results describe the relationship between BIS levels and responsiveness for commonly used volatile anesthetics, with and without opioids, across a range of anesthetic concentrations. The results of this study should be interpreted in light of the study design which included young, healthy adult volunteers with no sustained, noxious stimulation. These findings may not be generalizable to other populations or clinical situations.

papers.abstract: Although the interaction of sevoflurane, propofol, and opioids has been investigated regarding motor response to laryngoscopy, their hemodynamic impact during surgical stimulation remains unexplored. We therefore assessed the effect of sevoflurane, propofol, and remifentanil on the hemodynamic response to pneumoperitoneum and laparoscopic surgery. The American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I or II patients scheduled for elective laparoscopic surgery were randomly assigned to one of six groups with different combinations of sevoflurane-remifentanil, propofol-remifentanil, or sevoflurane-propofol-remifentanil, respectively. The Ce50 BARPP (pneumoperitoneum) for sevoflurane and propofol in combination with remifentanil was determined with the up-and-down method, and the interaction of the three drugs on mean arterial pressure (MAP) response was described with a linear-additive model. During surgery remifentanil was titrated to keep the MAP <100 mm Hg at fixed concentrations of sevoflurane (1 vol%), propofol (3 µg mL-1), or sevoflurane (0.5 vol%) plus propofol (1.5 µg mL-1). The relationship between remifentanil and MAP during surgery was described with a linear mixed-effects model. Data of 155 patients were analyzed. At remifentanil 5 ng mL-1 the Ce50 BARPP (95% CI) of sevoflurane was 1.56 (1.18-1.95) vol%, and of propofol 4.82 (4.29-5.36) µg mL-1. At remifentanil 3 ng/ml plus either propofol 1.8 µg mL-1 or sevoflurane 0.6 vol%, the values were 2.2 (2.0-2.4) vol% and 5.9 (5.7-6.0) µg mL-1. The drug interaction model revealed a propofol scaling factor (scaleSP) of 0.31 (0.19-0.44), representing the potency of propofol relative to sevoflurane, and a remifentanil constant kremi of 2.03 (0.82-3.24), representing the hypnotic-sparing effect of remifentanil. The median (interquartile range) of remifentanil during surgery was 6.4 (5.8-7.7), 4.9 (3.6-6.7), and 5.0 (3.7-6.0) ng mL-1 in groups SR, PR, and SPR, respectively. The MAP did not correlate with the remifentanil concentrations, demonstrating evidence for the drug titration paradox. The relative potency of sevoflurane to propofol in reducing the MAP response to pneumoperitoneum is similar to that for tolerance of laryngoscopy but differs from that for hypnotic endpoints. The effect of remifentanil on reducing the MAP response is similar whether it is combined with sevoflurane or propofol. Because titration to a dynamic clinical end point decouples the traditional relationship between drug input and clinical outcome, titration data cannot be used to validate pharmacodynamic models.

papers.abstract: Regional anesthesia provides significant perioperative benefits, including improved pain control and reduced opioid consumption. Clinical trial evidence underpins anesthetic practice, yet inadequate demographic representation and reporting may limit the ability to likely evaluate findings and perpetuate inequities. This systematic review assessed the reporting of race, ethnicity, and sex in randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of regional anesthesia for total joint arthroplasty (TJA). The Aggregate Analysis of Clinical Trials (AACT) database was searched for US-based interventional RCTs of regional anesthesia for TJA published from 2015 to 2025. Trials were required to be registered and published in English. Exclusion criteria included conference abstracts, duplicate publications, and non-peer-reviewed reports. Data on trial characteristics, sample size, interventions, and participant demographics were compared from published articles and ClinicalTrials.gov. The primary outcome was reporting of participant sex, race, and ethnicity in publications and registry entries. Secondary outcomes included demographic distributions across racial and ethnic groups and associations between reporting and study characteristics (funding source, year of publication, center type, US region, sample size) using Fisher's exact test. Twenty-nine RCTs were included in the final analysis, representing 2914 participants. Of 29 journal articles, 28 studies (96.6%) reported sex, 14 (48.3%) reported race, and five (17.2%) reported ethnicity in the published journal articles. Among studies reporting race, 1068 (78.5%) participants identified as White, 253 (18.6%) as Black, 30 (2.2%) as other, 6 (0.4%) as Asian or Pacific Islander, and one (0.07%) as Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander. Conversely, the data from ClinicalTrials.gov reveals that of the same 29 studies, 22 (75.9%) reported sex, 12 (41.4%) reported race, and seven (24.1%) reported ethnicity. Trial characteristics did not show statistically significant associations when comparing studies that did versus did not report race, ethnicity, or sex. In this review of demographic reporting of US-based regional anesthesia RCTs for TJA, sex was consistently reported, whereas race and ethnicity were infrequently captured. The lack of difference in reporting practices across various trial characteristics points toward a broader issue within the field of regional anesthesia for TJA. Notable inconsistencies in demographic reporting on ClinicalTrials.gov were also observed. The absence of standardized demographic reporting underscores the need for journals to mandate consistent reporting practices in clinical research. Efforts to recruit more diverse study populations are essential to enhance the applicability of trial results and to address ongoing inequities in access to care and patient outcomes following TJA.

papers.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies targeting the interleukin-23 pathway are effective in treating inflammatory bowel disease. However, these therapies must be administered intravenously or by subcutaneous injection. We conducted a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized trial of oral icotrokinra, a peptide that blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Participants were assigned to receive icotrokinra at a once-daily dose of 400 mg, 200 mg, or 100 mg or placebo. The primary end point was clinical response at week 12. Secondary end points included clinical remission, remission of symptoms, and endoscopic improvement at week 12. A total of 252 participants underwent randomization: 63 were assigned to the 400-mg group, 62 to the 200-mg group, 64 to the 100-mg group, and 63 to the placebo group. All the doses of icotrokinra were superior to placebo with respect to a clinical response at week 12, which occurred in 63% of the participants in the 400-mg group, 58% in the 200-mg group, and 55% in the 100-mg group, as compared with 27% in the placebo group (P<0.001 for all comparisons with placebo). The percentage of participants with clinical remission at week 12 was also significantly higher in the 400-mg group than in the placebo group (30% vs. 11%, P = 0.006), as were the percentage of participants with symptomatic remission (46% vs. 19%, P<0.001) and the percentage of participants with endoscopic improvement (37% vs. 14%, P = 0.002). Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 24% of the participants in the 200-mg group (P = 0.054 for the comparison with placebo); in accordance with the fixed-sequence testing procedure to account for multiple comparisons, no further formal testing of secondary end points was conducted. Through week 28, the percentage of participants with adverse events was 60% in the 400-mg group, 66% in the 200-mg group, 66% in the 100-mg group, and 62% in the placebo group. For serious adverse events, the percentages were 2%, 5%, 0%, and 10%, respectively. Among participants with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, a clinical response at week 12 was significantly more common with once-daily oral icotrokinra at each of three tested doses than with placebo. papers.abstract: In eastern and southern Africa, approximately 1 million people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and receiving oral therapy do not have viral suppression because of adherence challenges. We conducted a phase 3b, open-label, randomized trial to compare long-acting injectable cabotegravir plus rilpivirine with oral dolutegravir-based therapy among adults with virally suppressed HIV type 1 (viral load, <200 copies per milliliter) and suboptimal adherence or care engagement. The participants were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive intramuscular injections of cabotegravir (600 mg) plus rilpivirine (900 mg) every 8 weeks, with the first two injection visits occurring 4 weeks apart, or to continue daily oral dolutegravir-based therapy; baseline drug-resistance testing was not performed. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. Confirmed virologic failure (two consecutive viral loads of ≥200 copies per milliliter) was a key secondary end point. A total of 540 participants were enrolled across seven sites in Kenya, South Africa, and Uganda; 537 were included in the primary analysis. At 48 weeks, 244 of 268 participants (91.0%) in the long-acting-therapy group had a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter, as compared with 240 of 269 participants (89.2%) in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -3.1 to 6.9), which met the criterion for noninferiority. The results of a per-protocol analysis were consistent with those of the primary analysis. Confirmed virologic failure occurred in 5 participants (1.9%) in the long-acting-therapy group and in no participants in the oral-therapy group (risk difference, 1.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.3 to 3.5). Serious adverse events were reported in 11 of 271 participants (4.1%) who received long-acting therapy and in 8 of 269 participants (3.0%) who received oral therapy (risk difference, 1.1 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.1 to 4.2). Among persons with HIV in Africa who have adherence challenges, long-acting cabotegravir plus rilpivirine was noninferior to oral dolutegravir-based therapy for maintaining a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter. (Funded by Johnson & Johnson; IMPALA ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05546242; Pan African Clinical Trials Registry number, PACT202301600757432TMC278LAHTX3005.).

papers.abstract: Abstract While the field of precision oncology is rapidly expanding and more targeted options are revolutionizing cancer treatment paradigms, therapeutic resistance particularly to immunotherapy remains a pressing challenge. This can be largely attributed to the dynamic tumor-stroma interactions that continuously alter the microenvironment. While to date most advancements have been made through examining the clinical utility of tissue-based biomarkers, their invasive nature and lack of a holistic representation of the evolving disease in a real-time manner could result in suboptimal treatment decisions. Thus, using minimally-invasive approaches to identify biomarkers that predict and monitor treatment response as well as alert to the emergence of recurrences is of a critical need. Currently, research efforts are shifting towards developing liquid biopsy-based biomarkers obtained from patients over the course of disease. Liquid biopsy represents a unique opportunity to monitor intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment which could occur through the exchange of extracellular vesicles (EVs). EVs are lipid bilayer membrane nanoscale vesicles which transfer a plethora of biomolecules that mediate intercellular crosstalk, shape the tumor microenvironment, and modify drug response. The capture of EVs using innovative approaches, such as microfluidics, magnetic beads, and aptamers, allow their analysis via high throughput multi-omics techniques and facilitate their use for biomarker discovery. Artificial intelligence, using machine and deep learning algorithms, is advancing multi-omics analyses to uncover candidate biomarkers and predictive signatures that are key for translation into clinical trials. With the increasing recognition of the role of EVs in mediating immune evasion and as a valuable biomarker source, these real-time snapshots of cellular communication are promising to become an important tool in the field of precision oncology and spur the recognition of strategies to block resistance to immunotherapy. In this review, we discuss the emerging role of EVs in biomarker research describing current advances in their isolation and analysis techniques as well as their function as mediators in the tumor microenvironment. We also highlight recent lung cancer and melanoma studies that point towards their application as predictive biomarkers for immunotherapy and their potential clinical use in precision immuno-oncology.

papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer typically spreads via peritoneal seeding, hematogenous, or lymphatic routes. Bile duct metastasis is extremely rare, and peribiliary metastasis manifesting as diffuse Glissonian sheath infiltration without a detectable mass lesion, to our knowledge, has not been well documented. A 42-year-old woman with stage IVB high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, previously treated with cytoreductive surgery and multiple lines of chemotherapy, presented with fatigue, anorexia, and mild jaundice. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) revealed bile duct wall thickening, peribiliary edema (Glissonian sheath edema), and diffuse inflammatory changes without a discrete mass. Autoimmune and infectious workups were negative. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with biopsy showed micropapillary clusters of atypical cells. Immunohistochemistry was positive for CK7, CK19, PAX-8, P16, and mutant-type p53; CEA focally positive; ER negative; Ki-67 high. This confirmed metastatic high-grade serous carcinoma of ovarian origin involving the common bile duct wall. Imaging (MRI/MRCP) suggested diffuse peribiliary involvement compatible with Glissonian sheath infiltration, although the small biopsy did not directly sample the intrahepatic sheath itself. We hypothesize that the radiological changes reflect peribiliary lymphatic spread, but this remains an inference based on imaging-pathology correlation rather than a histologically proven mechanism. Effective biliary drainage could not be achieved because the patient was unable to tolerate the nasobiliary drain. She was discharged against medical advice and died shortly thereafter, according to family report. In cancer patients with unexplained cholestasis, peribiliary metastasis should be considered even when no mass is seen on cross-sectional imaging. ERCP with biopsy and immunohistochemistry are essential for diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Hereditary diffuse gastric cancer (HDGC) caused by germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in CDH1 remains a difficult hereditary cancer syndrome to manage. Prophylactic total gastrectomy has long been considered the most definitive preventive strategy, but recent penetrance estimates, expert endoscopic surveillance cohorts, and better characterization of early signet-ring cell lesions have challenged a uniform approach for all carriers. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on CDH1-associated gastric cancer risk, testing criteria, mechanisms of carcinogenesis, prophylactic gastrectomy, endoscopic surveillance, and emerging biomarkers for risk stratification. The available data support a more individualized discussion that integrates family history, age, comorbidity, sex-specific cancer risks, patient preferences, and access to expert surveillance. However, current biomarkers remain investigational, and no blood-, stool-, gastric-fluid-, or tissue-based assay is validated to replace surgery or endoscopic surveillance in routine care. At present, personalized management is best understood as structured shared decision-making within specialist centers, rather than fully biomarker-driven prevention. Future progress will require prospective registries, standardized surveillance protocols, molecular endpoints linked to clinical progression, and careful evaluation of quality of life after both surveillance and gastrectomy.

papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into pharmaceutical discovery, yet the extent to which AI-enabled assets have translated into clinical-stage programs remains incompletely characterized. We performed a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of therapeutic assets discovered or developed using AI approaches that had entered at least one interventional human clinical trial through March 1, 2026. We identified 129 AI-enabled therapeutic assets across 69 companies. Oncology was the dominant therapeutic area (74 assets, 57.3%), and small molecules accounted for the majority of the pipeline (103 assets, 79.8%). Among these assets, 72 (55.8%) had completed Phase 1 and 24 (18.9%) had completed Phase 2; only five had entered or completed Phase 3. The observed probability of success was 77.8% for Phase 1 and 19.5% for Phase 2. Forty-eight assets (37.2%) were classified as targeting a novel biological target. Among companies with available data, the median time from founding to Phase 1 entry was 6.5 years (IQR 4.0-9.2), median total funding raised was $186.7 million (IQR $48.1-$595.0 million), and the median employee count at clinical entry was 73 (IQR 32-129), with a median operational intensity of $2.72 million per employee. AI-enabled therapeutics are entering clinical testing at increasing scale, but most programs remain early in development, with few having advanced beyond Phase 2. This dataset provides a baseline for future evaluation of whether AI-enabled discovery ultimately improves regulatory approval rates and clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract: Objective: Our objective was to characterize the molecular–pathologic profile and recurrence patterns of endometrial cancer with pelvic lymph node isolated tumor cells (ITCs). Methods: A single-center retrospective study of patients with endometrial cancer and ITCs was conducted. Patients with concurrent lymph nodes or distant metastasis were excluded. Cases were reviewed by a gynecologic pathologist, and electronic medical records were reviewed. Descriptive statistics were performed using R 4.4.2. Results: A total of 43 patients were included, with a median follow-up time of 33 months. The majority were endometrioid carcinoma (91%) and stage I (72%). In total, 28 (65%) were MMR-proficient and p53-wild-type (MMRp p53wt), nine (21%) were MMR-deficient (MMRd), six (14%) were p53-abnormal (p53abn), and none were POLE-mutated (POLEmut). Additionally, 27 (96%) MMRp p53wt cases showed a microcystic, elongated, and fragmented (MELF) pattern of invasion. Adjuvant therapy was indicated in 38 (88%) patients; 32 (74%) received therapy and six (14%) declined. Four (9.3%) patients recurred, with a recurrence rate of 33% (2/6) for p53abn, 11% (1/9) for MMRd, and 4% (1/28) for MMRp p53wt. All recurrences were to distant sites. In the MMRp p53wt group, 16 (57%) had external beam radiation (EBRT) +/− vaginal brachytherapy (VBT), three (11%) had chemotherapy +/− radiation, and nine (32%) had no adjuvant treatment or VBT alone. Conclusions: Molecular profile is prognostically relevant in endometrial carcinoma with ITCs. ITCs in MMRp p53wt endometrioid carcinoma present a low risk of disease recurrence. As the majority of our cohort received adjuvant therapy, future work may explore de-escalating treatment in low-risk ITC cases.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), particularly with extramedullary disease (EMD), has a dismal prognosis. The efficacy and durability of allogeneic chimeric antigen receptor T cell (allo-CAR-T) therapy in this setting remain unclear. Methods Fourteen patients with post-transplant relapsed B-ALL received allogeneic anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, including eight with EMD. Clinical responses, survival, CAR-T kinetics, and toxicities were evaluated. Results With a median follow-up of 13.8 months (range, 4.4–52.9 months), the overall complete remission (CR) rate was 92.9% (13/14), with a median duration of remission (DOR) of 12.7 months (range, 3.5–50.3 months). Among patients with EMD, 87.5% (7/8) achieved CR, with a median DOR of 14.7 months (range, 3.5–50.3 months). Of the eight patients with EMD, four were Philadelphia chromosome-positive and received maintenance therapy with tyrosine kinase inhibitors after allo-CAR-T, including dasatinib ( n =1), ponatinib ( n =2), and olverembatinib ( n =1). Median overall survival and event-free survival were not reached in either the overall cohort or EMD subgroup. CAR-T cells persisted in vivo for a median of 5.9 months (range, 1.2–51.6 months). One patient experienced grade 3 cytokine release syndrome and grade 4 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome. One patient developed acute gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease, followed by chronic graft-versus-host disease involving the skin and lungs. Conclusion Allo-CAR-T therapy induces sustained remissions in patients with post-transplant relapsed B-ALL, including patients with EMD, and may serve as an effective backbone for tailored combination strategies. papers.abstract: Membrane-associated proliferating cell nuclear antigen (mPCNA) is an attractive tumor-selective antigen for antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) development. We generated a chimeric IgG1 ADC, RC14-MMAE, to exploit three key properties of mPCNA that support its use as an efficient delivery platform. First, flow-cytometric and imaging analyses show abundant mPCNA surface expression on multiple tumor cell lines and in JIMT1 xenografts, providing accessible epitopes for binding. Second, comparative profiling against non-malignant counterparts and normal mouse tissues reveals minimal or undetectable mPCNA at the plasma membrane of healthy cells, indicating a sharp tumor-normal differential expected to limit off-tumor targeting and improve the therapeutic window. Third, live-cell internalization assays demonstrate that RC14 rapidly accumulates in LAMP1-positive lysosomes after engaging mPCNA, confirming efficient trafficking along the endolysosomal pathway required for protease-mediated cleavage of the valine-citrulline linker and release of monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE). Consistent with this target profile, RC14-MMAE exhibits potent antigen-dependent cytotoxicity in mPCNA-positive tumor models in NSG mice, favorable pharmacokinetics, sustained payload retention in serum, robust in vivo antitumor activity with limited overt toxicity, and a significantly increased fraction of F4/80⁺ tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells within dissociated tumors. These findings establish mPCNA as a functionally validated, tumor-selective internalizing target and support RC14-MMAE as a first-in-class mPCNA-directed ADC with broad translational potential.

papers.abstract: Lower socioeconomic status conveys a known survival disadvantage for patients with esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC). The potential role of the treating center volume in mitigating this disparity has not been described to date. Non-metastatic EAC patients were identified (NCDB 2012-2021). High- and low-risk zip code groups were derived from income and education quartiles. Center volume was delineated as "low" or "high," with an annual threshold of ≥ 10 esophagectomies. Standard chi-square modeling, multivariable Cox hazard regression models, and Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were used where appropriate. Of 7462 EAC patients, 38.2% (n = 2849) resided in high-risk zip code areas, and 87.1% were treated at low-volume centers. Clinical (p = 0.230) and pathologic (p = 0.992) staging distribution did not differ across zip codes. High-volume centers saw a slightly increased proportion of advanced disease (p = 0.001). Patients at high-volume centers experienced better survival (5-year overall survival [5yOS], 44.97%) than their low-volume counterparts (5yOS, 40.62%) (p < 0.001). Patients residing in high-risk zip code areas demonstrated worse 5yOS than their low-risk counterparts (38.20% vs 43.74%; p < 0.001). Evaluation of low-volume centers showed that the high-risk zip code group had shorter survival than their low-risk counterparts (36.80% vs 43.21%; p < 0.001). Interestingly, in high-volume centers, survival across zip code groups was notably comparable (45.69% vs 46.20%; p = 0.80). Center expertise may offer an avenue for mitigating sociodemographic survival disparities in esophageal cancer. As discussions regarding centralized oncologic care continue, particular attention should be paid to the impact of high-volume center referral on the treatment of patients with social risk factors.

papers.abstract: Delayed diagnosis and treatment worsen survival in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Despite many potential causes, the influence of social determinants of health (SDoH) is understudied. We evaluated whether SDoH impact delays in diagnosis and treatment among patients who underwent resection for PDAC. Adults resected at a high-volume center were included (January 2016-November 2024). SDoH included insurance status, census-level income and education, rural-urban residence, and Area Deprivation Index. Primary endpoints were time from first imaging to histological diagnosis and time from first imaging to treatment initiation. Delay thresholds were derived using receiver operating characteristic analysis against overall survival. Uni- and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with delays, adjusting for demographic and clinical covariates, stratified by outpatient (OUP) versus emergency room (ER) presentation. Among 317 patients, the median age was 67 years, and 42.3% were female; 50.1% presented through ER. The median imaging-to-diagnosis interval was 11 days (interquartile [IQR] 3-27 days), and the median imaging-to-treatment interval was 40 days (IQR 27-59 days). In the OUP cohort, Medicare insurance was associated with delayed diagnosis compared with private insurance (OR 3.34 [95% CI 1.09-11.70]), whereas higher income was associated with up to 84% lower odds of delayed treatment. In the ER cohort, higher education was associated with reduced odds of delayed diagnosis (OR 0.27 [95% CI 0.07-0.88]) and delayed treatment (OR 0.33 [95% CI 0.11-0.91]). Post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) hospitalization predicted delays in the ER setting, whereas alarm symptoms reduced delays in both settings. papers.abstract: The five-year relative survival (RS) for cervical cancer in Puerto Rico and the United States (US) is less than 70%. To assess survival trends in the past decades, we compared the five-year RS of cervical cancer in Puerto Rico and in the US. Data was obtained from the Puerto Rico Central Cancer Registry and the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program. We included microscopically confirmed cases of cervical carcinoma between 2000 and 2021. The five-year RS trends were analyzed with Joinpoint regression models using the JPSurv software, which estimated the Average Absolute Change in Survival (AAC_S). Puerto Rico showed a lower five-year RS than US overall across the study period. In the US, the AAC_S was -0.78 for patients diagnosed between 2000 and 2003 (95%CI: -1.32 to -0.23), -0.22 for 2003-2013 (95%CI: -0.36 to -0.08), and 0.25 for 2013-2021 (95%CI: 0.01-0.49). In Puerto Rico, the AAC_S was -0.03 for 2000-2011 (95%CI: -0.56-0.51), 1.71 for 2011-2016 (95%CI: 0.60-2.83), and -1.10 for 2016-2021 (95%CI: -3.12-0.92). Puerto Rico shows poorer cervical cancer five-year RS than the US. Increased five-year RS was observed in the US overall population after 2013. In Puerto Rico, improvements in five-year RS were observed after 2011, but these were halted after 2016. This finding may suggest that barriers to accessing care during periods of extreme events, such as the convergence of the 2017 hurricanes and the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic challenges, likely affected survival trends from 2016 to 2021. Future research should further characterize barriers to improve cervical cancer survival.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background This cross‐sectional study aimed to identify symptom profiles and their associated factors in Chinese patients with multiple myeloma, thereby providing an evidence‐based foundation for developing targeted symptom management strategies. Methods Patients with multiple myeloma were recruited via convenience sampling from the hematology departments of three tertiary general hospitals in Zhejiang Province, China, between January and March 2024. Data collection utilized a sociodemographic and clinical characteristics questionnaire and the Chinese version of the M.D. Anderson Symptom Inventory‐Multiple Myeloma Module (MDASI‐MM) scale. The research conducted a latent profile analysis of symptom characteristics, followed by univariate analysis and multivariable multinomial logistic regression to examine factors associated with profile membership. Results The study included 265 Chinese patients with multiple myeloma. Latent profile analysis identified three distinct symptom profiles: “Low Symptom Burden with Walking Distress” (46.7%), “Moderate Physical Symptoms with Daily Life Interference” (37.9%), and “High Global Symptom Burden” (15.4%). Multinomial logistic regression analysis demonstrated that age, marital status, combination chemotherapy status, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status were significantly associated with symptom profile membership ( p < 0.05). Specifically, patients of advanced age and those with higher ECOG scores were more likely to belong to the higher burden profiles, while patients receiving combination chemotherapy and those who were unmarried/divorced/widowed were more likely to belong to the low‐burden profile. Conclusions Patients with multiple myeloma exhibit heterogeneous symptom experiences, classifiable into three latent profiles. Our findings suggest that age, marital status, combination chemotherapy, and ECOG performance status may help identify patients at risk for higher symptom burden. Future longitudinal research is needed to evaluate whether profile‐based interventions reduce symptom burden and improve quality of life.

papers.abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) is a complex autoimmune disease with distinct clinical and serological subtypes. Previous genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several susceptibility loci, particularly within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), but the broader genetic architecture and causal variants underlying AAV remain incompletely defined. We conducted a genome-wide association study including 2068 individuals with AAV and 3258 controls of European ancestry. The discovery cohort comprised a previously published GWAS dataset supplemented with newly recruited cases. Analyses were stratified by clinical (granulomatosis with polyangiitis [GPA] and microscopic polyangiitis [MPA]) and serological (proteinase 3-ANCA [PR3] and myeloperoxidase-ANCA [MPO]) subtypes. Findings were evaluated in an independent case cohort of 465 individuals. We performed conditional and joint analyses of the HLA region, functional fine-mapping, linkage disequilibrium score regression, and integrative multi-omics analyses to prioritise candidate causal variants and assess genetic correlations. We identified eight previously unreported loci and replicated four known loci associated with AAV at genome-wide significance. Within the HLA region, HLA-DPB1∗04 showed the strongest association with AAV, GPA, and PR3 subtypes, whereas HLA-DRB1∗04 was most strongly associated with MPO and MPA. Conditional analyses identified additional independent effects, including amino acid variation in HLA-DQA1. SNP-based heritability estimates indicated a substantial genetic contribution to AAV (h2 = 0·40). Genetic correlation analyses revealed shared heritability with multiple traits, including celiac disease and hypothyroidism. Integrative analyses highlighted candidate genes, including HCG9 and PRTN3, and implicated protein interaction networks involving genes related to neutrophil biology. Protein-protein interaction analysis identified networks involving genes implicated in AAV risk, including PRTN3, AZU1, ELANE, and SERPINA1. These findings expand the genetic landscape of AAV and support a complex and heterogeneous genetic architecture involving both MHC and non-MHC loci. The integration of genetic association, functional annotation, and network analyses suggests that disease susceptibility is mediated through multiple biological pathways, including immune regulation and neutrophil function. These insights may inform future mechanistic studies, improved disease stratification, and the development of targeted therapeutic strategies. papers.abstract: Canopy FGF signalling regulator 3 (CNPY3) is an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-resident chaperone essential for toll-like receptor (TLR) folding, trafficking and inflammasome activation. In rare paediatric cases, biallelic CNPY3 variants have been associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE), but available data remain sparse. 50 individuals from 38 unrelated families with biallelic CNPY3 variants and DEE were evaluated for exome and genome findings, standardised clinical phenotype descriptions, EEG results, and neuroimaging data. A selection of variants underwent functional analysis focussing on protein stability and localisation, TLR2 function, NLPR3 inflammasome activation, and structural conformation. Disease onset occurred in early infancy (median age at onset 68 days), with a clinical phenotype comprising global developmental delay (100%) and intractable epilepsy (86%), accompanied by microcephaly (70%), spasticity (77%), growth faltering (63%), stridor (48%), and early mortality (38%). Epileptic spasms and tonic seizures (46% each) were the most frequent seizure types, and EEG findings included suppression-burst (37%) and hypsarrhythmia (28%). Phenotypic severity varied substantially, with most patients being severely affected (median score 16, range 2-20). Most variants occurred in the homozygous state (95%), including 13 missense changes and 7 truncating alleles. Variants were classified as of uncertain significance (71%), followed by likely pathogenic (23%) and pathogenic (6%) according to ACMG/AMP criteria. Genotype-phenotype correlation showed that individuals with truncating variants were, on average, more severely affected than those with non-truncating variants (median score 18 vs 14.5). Protein modelling predicted conformational effects for most missense variants. In cells, frameshift alleles abolished CNPY3 protein expression, whereas nonsense alleles markedly reduced protein levels. ER localisation of CNPY3 remained preserved across tested genotypes; however, capacity to support TLR2 maturation and processing varied substantially. Remarkably, some missense variants permitted TLR2 surface expression but impaired downstream signalling and inflammasome activation, uncoupling trafficking from signal transduction. CNPY3-associated DEE is a severe early-onset disorder with genotype-dependent phenotypic severity, accompanied by allele-specific disruption of innate immune pathways. Our findings reveal separable effects on TLR trafficking, downstream signalling and inflammasome activation, identifying CNPY3 as a key regulator of multiple cellular pathways involved in inflammatory responses and neurodevelopment. papers.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual's deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span-wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

papers.abstract: The continuous antigenic evolution of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has repeatedly undermined the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies, underscoring the need for innovative approaches that improve therapeutic mAb breadth and durability of protection. Here, we engineered messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)-encoded bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) that, upon intravenous administration in lipid nanoparticles, achieved high serum concentrations, extended half-life, and serum neutralizing titers exceeding 1:10,000 in human neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)-expressing mice. To enhance resilience to viral escape, we used structure-guided computational design to introduce Fc modifications that promoted selective homodimerization, thereby enabling codelivery of multiple mRNA-encoded bsAbs with cognate heavy chain pairing. In vivo expression of a triple bsAb combination resulted in broad serum neutralization of historical and contemporary SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the highly mutated BA.3.2.2 lineage. Preexposure prophylaxis with the mRNA-delivered bsAb combination conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 challenge, preventing weight loss and decreasing viral burden in the lungs compared with vehicle control treatment. Together, the results provide proof of principle for mRNA-based delivery of Fc-engineered bsAb combinations to combat SARS-CoV-2 and potentially other rapidly evolving pathogens.

papers.abstract: The importance of gene-environment interactions (G × E) for complex human traits is heavily debated. Recently, biobank-based genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have revealed many statistically significant G × E signals, though most lack clear evidence of biological significance. Here, we partly explain this discrepancy by showing that many G × E signals simplify to additive effects on a different phenotype scale, a classical concern that is currently underappreciated. Our results clearly distinguish G × sex effects on height, which vanish on the log scale, from G × sex effects on testosterone, where the log scale uncovers biologically meaningful female-specific effects. Across 32 phenotypes in UK Biobank, we find that scaling by a power transformation can explain 45% of polygenic score (PGS) × sex interactions and that simple log transformation can explain 23%, with similar results for other environments. We also show that the phenotype scale can substantially impact GWAS discovery and the construction and evaluation of polygenic scores. Finally, we provide a set of guidelines to consider and choose phenotype scales in modern genetic studies.

papers.abstract: Fluid therapy is ubiquitous in the intensive care unit (ICU) but carries risks, especially in mechanically ventilated patients. Contemporary global practice across dose, indication, and type is unknown. To characterize ICU fluid practices in mechanically ventilated adults. International prospective observational cohort study between April 2024 and July 2025, across 206 ICUs in 41 countries on 6 continents. Consecutive adult patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation within 3 days of ICU admission and ventilated 24 hours or more. Exclusion criteria were age younger than 16 years and transfer under mechanical ventilation from another ICU. Fluid volume, indication, and type after intubation. Key measures included (1) total infused volume and daily fluid balance over 7 days after intubation; (2) the indication for fluid therapy over the first 3 days after intubation; (3) the proportion of total administered fluid volume attributable to each fluid type over the first 3 days after intubation. Among 2454 patients analyzed (median age, 63 years [IQR, 49-73 years]; 63.6% [1560] male), median daily fluid input peaked on day 1 at 3.0 L (IQR, 2.2-4.0 L) and declined to 2.6 L (IQR, 1.8-3.5 L) through day 6. Daily fluid balance (median, 0.9 L; IQR, 0.1-1.9 L on day 1) decreased to less than 0.3 L (IQR, -0.5 to 1.2 L) by day 3 and remained near-neutral through day 6. Maintenance and replacement fluids (to meet daily requirements and to correct ongoing losses; 31.9%) and creep fluids (to deliver medications and maintain catheter patency; 30.9%) were the primary indications, whereas resuscitation (to restore circulating blood volume; 16.0%) accounted for a smaller proportion. Isotonic balanced crystalloids (48.9%) and isotonic saline (0.9% sodium chloride) (27.0%) were common; colloids were rare (1.3%). Substantial between-site variation persisted after adjustment for case-mix. In this prospective international cohort study, fluid therapy varied widely among mechanically ventilated critically ill patients, with maintenance and creep fluids-rather than resuscitation fluids-accounting for most total volume.

papers.abstract: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain. In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90. The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group. Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. papers.abstract: Spirocyclic frameworks, polycyclic structures in which two rings share a single carbon atom, constitute key structural motifs across diverse areas, including optoelectronic and hole-transporting materials1-3, ligand design for coordination complexes4-6, and numerous natural products7. In a spiro skeleton, the two molecular units adopt an orthogonal arrangement, generating a rigid three-dimensional (3D) architecture. Introducing a single carbon atom to join two components to form the spiro centre therefore represents a direct strategy for constructing such frameworks. Previous carbon-atom-transfer approaches have largely relied on π-bond reactivity, whereas controlled insertion of a carbon atom into C-C σ-bonds remains challenging8-11. Here we report a rhodium-catalysed spiro-carbon-atom insertion reaction that converts biphenylene substrates into spirocyclic structures through sequential C-C bond activation. Using N-isocyanoiminophosphorane (PINC)12-14 as an atomic carbon equivalent, the reaction forms four new C-C bonds at a spiro centre. The transformation enables both homo- and cross-spirofusion of biphenylenes and can be extended to reactions combining σ- and π-bond activation. These results establish a catalytic strategy for constructing structurally complex spirocyclic frameworks through C-C σ-bond activation, with a single carbon atom serving as a central linchpin.

papers.abstract: The outcome of Philadelphia-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph-positive ALL) has greatly improved with the use of tyrosine kinase inhibitors and immunotherapy. In this trial, we randomly assigned adult patients with Ph-positive ALL in a 2:1 ratio to receive ponatinib plus blinatumomab (intervention group) or imatinib plus chemotherapy (control group) as frontline treatment. A crossover to the intervention group was allowed for patients with persistence or reappearance of measurable residual disease in the control group. The primary end point was event-free survival. A total of 236 patients underwent randomization: 158 to the intervention group and 78 to the control group. The median age of the patients was 55 years (range, 24 to 82). At a median follow-up of 23.7 months, the estimated 24-month event-free survival was 86% in the intervention group and 67% in the control group (P<0.001). Survival with no measurable residual disease was 68% and 42%, respectively. At the end of induction, a complete hematologic response was observed in 94% of the patients in the intervention group and in 79% of those in the control group. After blinatumomab consolidation, a molecular response was observed in 71% and 49% of the patients, respectively. After crossover to the intervention group, 20 of 31 patients (64%) had a molecular response. Overall survival was 90% in the intervention group and 85% in the control group. The cumulative incidence of relapse was 5% and 13%, respectively. As of this report, only 19% of the patients in the intervention group had undergone hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation after having had a first complete hematologic response. In this phase 3 trial, a frontline chemotherapy-free targeted and immunotherapeutic approach was superior to the use of imatinib and chemotherapy. papers.abstract: Radiotherapy confers a later risk of secondary malignancies, including radiation-associated breast cancer. Distinctive molecular profiles emerge in tumors from pre-irradiated tumor beds, but effects on therapeutic options remain understudied. We developed a murine model of radiation-associated breast cancer by transplanting p53-mutant mammary HC11 epithelial cells that had been previously exposed to radiation (HC11RT) into mammary fat pads (MFP) that had been previously irradiated. Tumor incidence from HC11RT cells increased two-fold when grown in irradiated MFP. Compared to tumors grown in sham-irradiated MFP, tumors from irradiated MFP had elevated TGFβ in both tumor and CD8+ T cells and elevated PD-L1 on CD4+ T cells, resulting in improved response to immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI). This study provides evidence that prior irradiation potentiates tumorigenesis and immune evasion through both tumor cell autonomous and non-autonomous mechanisms. As a result, radiation-associated cancers may exhibit greater response to ICI than tumors of the same histology that are not associated with prior radiotherapy.

papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have changed the treatment landscape of pleural mesothelioma (PM) over the past decade. This review summarizes the history of immunotherapy in PM, covering studies of single-agent immunotherapy, combination checkpoint blockade, the integration of ICIs into frontline therapeutic strategies, and ICI-VEGF combinations. Also discussed are the emerging role of biomarkers in guiding first-line therapy selection for patients with PM and novel therapeutic approaches. Dual checkpoint blockade targeting PD-1 and CTLA-4 demonstrated clinical efficacy in early-phase studies and led to the pivotal phase III CheckMate 743 trial, which established nivolumab and ipilimumab as a standard first-line systemic therapy for PM, particularly in patients with nonepithelioid histology. Since that time, other combination therapy approaches have been explored. For example, chemoimmunotherapy studies have evaluated ICIs, including pembrolizumab and durvalumab, in combination with platinum chemotherapy, with pembrolizumab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy expanding the approved frontline treatment options for PM. VEGF inhibition, validated in the phase III MAPS study, provided a biologic rationale for combining antiangiogenic agents with ICIs. This prompted investigation of bevacizumab in combination with atezolizumab and chemotherapy in the BEAT-meso study. Unfortunately, this combination did not provide meaningful benefit in this setting. Optimal patient selection and treatment sequencing remain undefined. Although robust data support the use of second-line immunotherapy after first-line chemotherapy, there is a paucity of evidence regarding the efficacy of chemotherapy following frontline ICI. Despite advancements in therapeutic options in PM, biomarker-driven treatment selection remains limited at this time. Future large clinical studies must incorporate validated and standardized biomarker subanalyses, including approaches such as circulating tumor DNA and multiomics, for biomarkers to become clinically relevant in this heterogeneous malignancy. Finally, novel therapeutic strategies, including bispecific antibodies, targeted therapies, perioperative immunotherapy, vaccines, and cellular therapies, are under active investigation and may further expand treatment options for patients with PM.

papers.abstract: Abstract High-dose vitamin C (HDVC) exhibits antitumor and immunomodulatory properties and may enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs); however, its ability to reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in pancreatic cancer, particularly through modulating tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) polarization, remains unclear. In this study, the antitumor activity of HDVC was evaluated in a subcutaneous KPC mouse model, while in vitro models utilizing lipopolysaccharide (LPS) + IFN-γ-stimulated mouse and human macrophages were employed to investigate polarization. Mechanisms were probed by RNA sequencing, western blotting, flow cytometry, pharmacological inhibition, and siRNA-mediated JAK2 knockdown. Macrophage involvement was confirmed in vivo via clodronate liposome-mediated depletion, and the combinatory effect of HDVC with anti-PD-1 therapy was assessed. The results showed that HDVC significantly inhibited pancreatic tumor growth and prolonged survival in vivo. Mechanistically, HDVC enhanced LPS + IFN-γ-induced M1 macrophage polarization, at least in part through activation of the JAK2-STAT1 signaling pathway, without markedly increasing M2-associated features. The antitumor efficacy of HDVC was markedly attenuated upon macrophage depletion, supporting the involvement of macrophage-dependent immune modulation. Furthermore, HDVC enhanced the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, accompanied by increased M1-like macrophages and CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration in the TME. These findings identify HDVC as a potential immunomodulator that remodels the immunosuppressive TME of pancreatic cancer through macrophage-centered immune remodeling, providing a rationale for further investigating HDVC-based combination strategies with ICIs in pancreatic cancer.

papers.abstract: Metformin is a potential anticancer agent; however, evidence of benefit in endometrial neoplasia is limited. We evaluated whether adding metformin improved the outcomes of progestin-based fertility-sparing treatment. In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, phase IIb trial using blinded central adjudication, women aged 18-42years with an institutional diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) or presumed stage IA grade 1 endometrioid carcinoma were assigned (1:1:1) to medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) alone, MPA plus metformin 750mg/day, or MPA plus metformin 1500mg/day. Central pathological review reclassified baseline specimens according to the 2020 World Health Organization criteria and adjudicated remission and recurrence. The primary endpoint was the 3-year recurrence-free survival (RFS) rate from treatment initiation. Secondary endpoints included remission, pregnancy outcomes, and safety. Analysis included 154 patients. Median body mass index was 24.3 (range, 15.6-57.1) kg/m2. The Kaplan-Meier estimates of the 3-year RFS rate were 44.7% with MPA alone and 44.5% with the pooled metformin groups. The prespecified log-rank test showed no significant difference (P=0.825). Remission rates were 54.0%, 58.8%, and 50.9% in the MPA-alone, metformin 750mg, and metformin 1500mg groups, respectively. Among the 57 women who attempted to conceive, pregnancy occurred in 36.8%, 57.9%, and 42.1%, and live birth in 31.6%, 52.6%, and 31.6%, respectively. Metformin increased gastrointestinal adverse events and was associated with less MPA-associated weight gain; no new safety signals emerged. Adding metformin to MPA did not improve RFS or remission rates, suggesting limited benefit in fertility-sparing treatment of endometrial neoplasia.

papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitors presents a major clinical challenge in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study aims to elucidate the epigenetic mechanisms underlying PD-1 inhibitor resistance, with a specific focus on the expression profiles of PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) and their associated signaling networks. High-throughput RNA sequencing was performed on matched pre- and post-resistance plasma samples from three NSCLC patients to identify differentially expressed piRNAs. The top five candidate piRNAs were selected for subsequent verification. Plasma piRNA levels and comprehensive clinical data from an independent cohort of 50 NSCLC patients (evaluated at both pre- and post-resistance stages) were analyzed. Downstream target genes of the candidate piRNAs were predicted using TargetScan and miRanda algorithms, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) functional enrichment analyses. Target gene expression was experimentally validated via quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Spearman's rank correlation was utilized to assess the relationship between piRNA expression and systemic inflammatory indices. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Five candidate piRNAs (Hsap_2765751, Hsap_249, Hsap_1847317, Hsap_681799, and Hsap_857420) exhibited significant differential expression. Notably, Hsap_1847317 was robustly upregulated following the development of resistance (P < 0.001). Bioinformatic and experimental analyses implicated Hsap_1847317 is implicated in the Wnt signaling pathway, while qRT-PCR demonstrated significantly higher AXIN2 mRNA expression after resistance (P < 0.001). these associative data do not establish direct regulation. Furthermore, the systemic neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) significantly increased during the resistance phase (P < 0.001) and exhibited a positive correlation with Hsap_1847317 expression (r = 0.395, P = 0.005). ROC curve analysis demonstrated excellent predictive efficacy, yielding an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.944 for Hsap_1847317 and 0.720 for NLR in this cohort. Our findings indicate that plasma Hsap_1847317 and NLR are candidate non-invasive biomarkers for monitoring acquired resistance to PD-1 inhibitors in NSCLC. This study association between Hsap_1847317, Wnt-related enrichment, and AXIN2 mRNA provides a hypothesis for further mechanistic testing rather than evidence of a causal Hsap_1847317/Wnt/AXIN2 axis.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer characterized by high molecular heterogeneity and a lack of effective targeted therapies. Increasing evidence indicates that metabolic reprogramming and redox homeostasis are critical determinants of TNBC progression; however, the transcriptional mechanisms linking these processes to mitochondrial function remain incompletely understood. In this study, integrative bioinformatics analyses identified nuclear receptor subfamily 3 group C member 2 (NR3C2) as a potential regulatory factor in TNBC. NR3C2 expression was significantly decreased in TNBC and was associated with patient prognosis. Functional assays demonstrated that NR3C2 overexpression markedly inhibited cell proliferation and migration in vitro and suppressed tumor growth and dissemination in zebrafish xenograft models. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing identified NDUFB3, an accessory subunit of mitochondrial complex I, as a downstream target of NR3C2. Dual-luciferase reporter assays further confirmed that NR3C2 directly regulates NDUFB3 transcription. Functional analyses revealed that NR3C2 modulates mitochondrial activity, as evidenced by increased mitochondrial membrane potential and complex I activity, accompanied by reduced ATP production and elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. Notably, NR3C2-induced ROS accumulation promoted apoptosis, whereas these effects were partially reversed by NDUFB3 knockdown or treatment with the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine (NAC). Consistently, in vivo experiments demonstrated that NR3C2 suppresses tumor growth and metastasis in a ROS-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings indicate that NR3C2 inhibits TNBC progression by regulating mitochondrial function and ROS homeostasis, at least in part through NDUFB3. This study provides new insights into the interplay between transcriptional regulation and mitochondrial redox balance and highlights NR3C2 as a potential therapeutic target for TNBC.

papers.abstract: Chemotherapy non-response remains a major challenge in bladder cancer, yet the endothelial states and intercellular communication programs associated with treatment failure remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic data, computational analyses, and in vitro experiments to characterize endothelial programs associated with chemotherapy response. A non-response-related transcriptional program was preferentially enriched in endothelial cells and was most prominent in the TipEC_2 tip-like endothelial subset. Integrative analyses identified DLL4 as a key feature of this endothelial state. Spatial and ligand-receptor analyses further supported a DLL4-associated tip-like endothelial niche and inferred DLL4-NOTCH3-related communication between endothelial and malignant compartments, together with RBPJ-associated transcriptional activity in DLL4-positive TipEC_2 cells. Consistently, cisplatin-resistant bladder cancer cells showed increased expression of NOTCH3 and downstream transcriptional targets, whereas pharmacological Notch inhibition suppressed downstream HES1 and HEY1 expression and partially restored cisplatin sensitivity. Elevated DLL4 expression was associated with chemotherapy non-response and unfavorable survival. In a separate prognostic analysis, a DLL4-positive TipEC_2-associated risk model stratified patients by overall survival in TCGA-BLCA and GSE13507. Collectively, these findings identify a DLL4-associated tip-like endothelial niche linked to chemotherapy non-response and suggest DLL4-NOTCH3 signaling as a potential molecular link between vascular remodeling and treatment resistance in bladder cancer.

papers.abstract: Metal ions serve as key regulators of the dynamic equilibrium within the tumor microenvironment (TME). In recent years, the TME has emerged as a central regulatory hub for tumor initiation, progression, and metastasis; its complexity has become both a frontier and a major challenge in oncology research. Current therapies are often constrained by immune tolerance, metabolic heterogeneity, and microenvironment-mediated escape mechanisms, necessitating breakthroughs in novel targets and strategies. Metal ions, functioning as enzyme cofactors, signaling molecules, and redox regulators, profoundly affect tumor progression by modulating redox homeostasis, immune responses, and metabolic reprogramming. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in metal ion-mediated regulation of the TME. It focuses on elucidating the multidimensional mechanisms by which metal ions facilitate immunogenic remodeling and metabolic interactions, and prospectively explores innovative metal-ion-based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. It further highlights the potential of personalized metal metabolomics to advance precision oncology and facilitate the clinical translation of metal ion-based theranostic strategies.

papers.abstract: Prolonged colonic inflammation and ulcerative colitis lead to colon cancer. The rapid growth and treatment-resistant nature of these tumors are primarily influenced by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which is led by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). However, factors influencing or regulating the immunosuppressive nature of TAMs have not been sufficiently studied. In this manuscript, we use a mouse model of colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CRC) to demonstrate that WNT expression in TAMs regulates their immunosuppressive function by inhibiting Glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3β) within the macrophages, possibly through an autofeedback loop. GSK3β is a positive regulator of PD-1 and PD-L1 expression in macrophages and promotes an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therefore, GSK-3β inhibition alters the immunosuppressive nature of the immune microenvironment and effectively controls tumor growth. In Csf1r.iCre; Porcnfl/fl mice, the absence of macrophage-derived WNT promotes tumor growth in the model of colitis-associated colon cancer. Absence of macrophage-derived WNT stabilizes GSK-3β in macrophages and promotes an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. We also show that pharmacological inhibition of GSK-3β in a macrophage-specific manner, achieved by systemic delivery of a lipo-GSK3β inhibitor, effectively inhibits tumor growth. Therefore, this manuscript demonstrates for the first time that the macrophage-specific modulation of GSK3β can be a potential target to treat colitis-associated colon cancer.
